**The four questions.** (1) A second call: one drop per attempt however often it is reported; a failed connect is reported once and never also as a drop. (2) An empty input: a connect with no cap is capped at the ceiling's; a URL with no host or port does not plan; no glue files yet report SKIPPED, never a vacuous pass. (3) After an interruption: a host that does not resolve is unresolved, not bad parameters; the TLS closer's IOException off the main thread is swallowed and nothing else is. (4) Another mode, orientation or language: the encoded rotation is the side the accelerometer read, never the display's, fixed for the broadcast.

## Batch C4a — the bridge core and the JVM host

The suite is the core's (`./gradlew test`, which now includes the `host` subproject), plus the host's smoke run in Task 21.

### Task 20: `BridgeCore` — the engine host every platform uses

Carries 1, 12, 14, 15, 17, 18 and 27, CD7, CD9, CD11, CD31 (rewritten as the pair notice), CD32, CD33 and CD37, and the amendment's platform duties: the install's phone id and the A17 records in app-private storage, readiness reported by the platform and replayed into every new pairing, and the capture opened only while it is wanted. `BridgeCore` joins the engine to a `Platform`, and this is the one place where the rules from Tasks 10–19 meet. The Android glue (Task 33) and the JVM host (Task 21) are both thin `Platform`s around it, so every rule here is JVM-tested once and runs unchanged on the phone.

Pre-flight findings folded here: **P5** (plan C's `SessionConfig ===` mutant was equivalent, `SessionConfig` having no `equals`): `PairRequest` is a plain class too (Task 2), so the pair notice compares by identity on purpose, and its mutant is now `name ==`, which the re-pair test kills. **P6** (org.json's `getInt` coerces `3.0`): the log test reads `line.get("count")`. **P11** (a failure posted for the arm never reached `armFailed`): `pairFailed(request, t)` is the one way back for work the platform posted, with the identity check, and Task 33's capture build reports through it.

Capture is wanted while a broadcast is held, or while the engine is Paired and the viewfinder is shown.** The amendment (_Readiness_) has the camera and mic open on the viewfinder and closed while waiting with the phone locked or the app elsewhere, and a go-live opening them from the service. `BridgeCore` decides; the platform builds and tears down. ```kotlin
package com.seazn.capture.engine.adapter

import com.seazn.capture.engine.core.Command
import com.seazn.capture.engine.core.LinkCounters
import com.seazn.capture.engine.core.PairRequest

/** What a platform gives `BridgeCore`. Android's is the glue (Task 33); the JVM host's is scripted (Task 21). */
interface Platform {
  /** Carry out one command. Never blocks the calling (scheduler) thread; outcomes come back through BridgeCore. */
  fun execute(command: Command)

  /** One HTTP request, answered once on any thread. */
  fun http(request: HttpRequest, answer: (HttpOutcome) -> Unit)

  /**
   * CD37: open ([wanted]) or close the camera and microphone. Called on the scheduler thread, only on
   * a change. Must return at once: a build posted elsewhere that fails reports through
   * [BridgeCore.pairFailed] with [request], the pairing it was built for (P11).
   */
  fun capture(wanted: Boolean, request: PairRequest?)

  /** Cumulative counts for the attempt, or null when it is not the attempt the endpoint holds. */
  fun frames(attemptId: Int): FrameCount?

  fun link(attemptId: Int): LinkCounters?

  /** Read at every publish, on the scheduler thread. Volatile reads only. */
  fun facts(): PlatformFacts

  fun snapshot(wire: Map<String, Any?>)

  fun recordLine(line: String)

  /** CD8: the intent numbered [seq] has run, with every snapshot and line it caused. Emitted as an event. */
  fun acked(seq: Int)
}

/**
 * App-private storage, excluded from backup (amendment, _Pairing, takeover and rejoin_): Android's
 * `noBackupFilesDir`, the JVM host's temporary folder. Scheduler thread only.
 */
interface PrivateStore {
  fun read(name: String): String?

  /** Durable before it returns: A17's record is written before the `End` that follows it. */
  fun write(name: String, text: String)

  fun delete(name: String)
}
```

`K/adapter/PairingStore.kt`:

```kotlin
package com.seazn.capture.engine.adapter

import com.seazn.capture.engine.core.Json
import com.seazn.capture.engine.core.PairingName
import com.seazn.capture.engine.core.PhoneFacts
import com.seazn.capture.engine.core.RecordEntry
import com.seazn.capture.engine.core.StoppedRecord

/**
 * The install's phone id and the A17 records. The id is random, made once and kept, not derived from
 * hardware, and not a secret. Records are one JSON object per line. A file no rule can read is
 * reported through [problem] and read as empty: never a silent loss (AGENTS §13, class 3).
 */
class PairingStore(
  private val store: PrivateStore,
  private val newId: () -> String,
  private val problem: (RecordEntry) -> Unit,
) {
  fun phone(appVersion: String, model: String): PhoneFacts {
    val kept = store.read(PHONE_ID)?.trim()?.takeIf { it.isNotEmpty() }
    val id = kept ?: newId().also { store.write(PHONE_ID, it) }
    return PhoneFacts(id, appVersion, model)
  }

  /** This code and slot's current record, pruning the rest past `keepUntil` (RR2). */
  fun stopped(name: PairingName, nowWallMs: Long): StoppedRecord? {
    val all = records()
    val kept = StoppedRecord.pruned(all, nowWallMs)
    if (kept.size != all.size) save(kept)
    return kept.lastOrNull { it.isFor(name) }
  }

  fun write(record: StoppedRecord) = save(records().filterNot { it.code == record.code && it.slot == record.slot } + record)

  fun delete(code: String, slot: Int) = save(records().filterNot { it.code == code && it.slot == slot })

  private fun records(): List<StoppedRecord> =
    store.read(STOPPED).orEmpty().lines().filter { it.isNotBlank() }.mapNotNull { line ->
      parse(line) ?: null.also { problem(RecordEntry("store-unreadable", listOf("file" to STOPPED))) }
    }

  private fun parse(line: String): StoppedRecord? =
    try {
      val map = JsonReader.parse(line) as? Map<*, *> ?: return null
      StoppedRecord(
        map["code"] as? String ?: return null,
        (map["slot"] as? Double)?.toInt() ?: return null,
        map["sid"] as? String ?: return null,
        (map["stoppedAt"] as? Double)?.toLong() ?: return null,
        (map["keepUntil"] as? Double)?.toLong() ?: return null,
      )
    } catch (_: JsonReader.Malformed) {
      null
    }

  private fun save(records: List<StoppedRecord>) {
    if (records.isEmpty()) return store.delete(STOPPED)
    store.write(STOPPED, records.joinToString("\n") { Json.obj(listOf("code" to it.code, "slot" to it.slot, "sid" to it.sid, "stoppedAt" to it.stoppedAtEpochMs, "keepUntil" to it.keepUntilEpochMs)) })
  }

  companion object {
    const val PHONE_ID = "phone-id"
    const val STOPPED = "stopped-records"
  }
}
```

`OwnedSlot` is plan C's, unchanged:

```kotlin
package com.seazn.capture.engine.adapter

/**
 * CD32: one value, owned by whoever took it last. A module instance takes the slot in `OnCreate` and
 * releases it in `OnDestroy`. A release by an owner that has since been replaced changes nothing, so
 * a JS reload never clears the new instance's listener, whichever of the two runs first.
 */
class OwnedSlot<T : Any> {
  private var owner: Any? = null

  @Volatile
  var value: T? = null
    private set

  @Synchronized
  fun take(by: Any, value: T) {
    owner = by
    this.value = value
  }

  @Synchronized
  fun release(by: Any) {
    if (owner !== by) return
    owner = null
    value = null
  }
}
```

**`BridgeCore`**, in full. Each function stays within 10–25 lines (AGENTS §12).

```kotlin
package com.seazn.capture.engine.adapter

import com.seazn.capture.engine.core.*
import kotlin.math.abs

/**
 * The engine host every platform uses (CD3). Intents in, commands out, snapshots and record lines
 * up. Every rule from Tasks 10–19 meets here, so the Android glue and the JVM host are both thin.
 * Every input is posted, so the poller, the machine and the notices see inputs in one order.
 */
class BridgeCore(
  private val clock: Clock,
  scheduler: Scheduler,
  private val platform: Platform,
  store: PrivateStore,
  private val appVersion: String,
  private val model: String,
  newId: () -> String = { java.util.UUID.randomUUID().toString() },
) {
  private val guarded = GuardedScheduler(scheduler, ::failed)
  private val record = SessionRecord { line -> platform.recordLine(line) }
  private val sticky = StickyFailure(CommandSink(::route), ::report)
  private val pollers = AttemptPollers(guarded, ::frames, platform::link, ::report)
  private val ticks = TickLateness()
  private val gaps = FrameGaps()
  private val engine = Engine(clock, guarded, sticky, SnapshotSink(::published), record)
  private val pairings = PairingStore(store, newId) { engine.log(it) }
  private val phone by lazy { pairings.phone(appVersion, model) }

  /** The pairing the last notice saw, by identity (P5): a re-scan of the same code is a new pairing. */
  private var noticed: PairRequest? = null

  /** CD37. Scheduler thread only, but for [viewfinder], which is volatile. */
  private var captureWanted = false

  /** The pairing the capture was last opened for, by identity: its failures report against it (P11). */
  private var capturedFor: PairRequest? = null

  @Volatile private var viewfinder = false

  /** The platform's latest readiness, and the last one sent to the machine. Scheduler thread only. */
  private var readiness = Readiness.UNKNOWN
  private var sent: Readiness? = null

  @Volatile private var checkedAtMs: Long? = null

  /** The last published snapshot's language (P3), for the glue's notification. */
  @Volatile private var language: String? = null

  /** Review Focus 2: an answer before the first tick, so a restarted JS never reads nothing. */
  @Volatile private var current: Map<String, Any?> = wire(Projection.snapshot(Phase.Idle(), clock.now()), PlatformFacts())

  /** Carry 15: the tick starts on the scheduler thread. */
  fun start() {
    guarded.schedule(0) { engine.start() }
  }

  /**
   * An intent from JS, mapped on the scheduler thread (the phone id and the A17 record are read from
   * storage there). With a `seq`, the ack is posted after the input's own tasks, so it reaches JS
   * after everything the input caused and before any later tick's snapshot (CD8).
   */
  fun send(intent: Map<String, Any?>) {
    guarded.schedule(0) {
      val input = IntentMapping.input(intent, phone) { name -> pairings.stopped(name, clock.wallMs()) }
      if (input != null) report(input) else engine.log(RecordEntry("intent-unknown", listOf("intent" to intent["kind"] as? String)))
      WireValues.int(intent["seq"])?.let { seq -> guarded.schedule(0) { platform.acked(seq) } }
    }
  }

  /** From any thread. The notices run after the machine has run the input, never inside the snapshot sink (CD31). */
  fun report(input: Input) {
    guarded.schedule(0) { pollers.onInput(input) }
    engine.send(input)
    guarded.schedule(0) { notice() }
  }

  /** From any thread: a failure the glue caught on its own scope (CD9). */
  fun failure(t: Throwable) {
    guarded.schedule(0) { failed(t) }
  }

  /**
   * From any thread (P11): work the platform posted for [request]'s pairing failed, such as the
   * capture build. It ends that pairing fatal-error and named, sticky for the process when permanent
   * and for the pairing otherwise (CD11). A failure for a pairing no longer held, by identity, is only
   * recorded: it must never end a newer one.
   */
  fun pairFailed(request: PairRequest, t: Throwable) {
    guarded.schedule(0) {
      if (engine.phase.pairing?.request !== request || engine.phase is Phase.Ended) {
        engine.log(RecordEntry("pair-step-late", listOf("error" to t.javaClass.simpleName)))
      } else {
        val scope = if (Failures.permanent(t)) Scope.PROCESS else Scope.PAIRING
        sticky.fail(Failures.describe(t), engine.phase.attemptInHand, scope)
      }
    }
  }

  /**
   * From any thread (I4, A11): the capture for [request] could not open because another app holds
   * the camera. That is not ready, camera, never an end: the pairing stays, the engine reads the
   * camera taken while paired or held (Task 7), and the release the platform sees opens it again
   * through `ReopenCamera`. Checked by identity like [pairFailed]; a late one is only recorded.
   */
  fun cameraBusy(request: PairRequest) {
    guarded.schedule(0) {
      if (engine.phase.pairing?.request !== request || engine.phase is Phase.Ended) {
        engine.log(RecordEntry("pair-step-late", listOf("error" to "camera-busy")))
      } else {
        engine.log(RecordEntry("camera-busy", emptyList()))
        report(Input.CameraContended)
      }
    }
  }

  /**
   * From any thread (CD21): the platform could not ask for the permissions at all (no activity, or a
   * request already in flight). The pairing still asking ends fatal-error and named, so the operator
   * taps to pair again. It is never read as a refusal, whose panel would tell the operator to change
   * a setting they never saw. With no pairing asking, it is only recorded.
   */
  fun askFailed(t: Throwable) {
    guarded.schedule(0) {
      if (engine.phase !is Phase.Pairing) {
        engine.log(RecordEntry("pair-step-late", listOf("error" to t.javaClass.simpleName)))
      } else {
        sticky.fail(Failures.describe(t), engine.phase.attemptInHand, Scope.PAIRING)
      }
    }
  }

  /** P3: the notification's language, the pairing's until `setLanguage` replaces it; null with no pairing. Any thread. */
  fun language(): String? = language

  /** From any thread (A11): the platform's facts; null leaves a fact as it was. Sent only when a check changes. */
  fun readiness(cameraFrames: Boolean? = null, audioPeak: Double? = null, pose: Pose? = null) {
    guarded.schedule(0) {
      readiness = readiness.copy(cameraFrames = cameraFrames ?: readiness.cameraFrames, audioPeak = audioPeak ?: readiness.audioPeak, pose = pose ?: readiness.pose)
      val last = sent
      if (last == null || last.cameraFrames != readiness.cameraFrames || last.sound != readiness.sound || last.pose != readiness.pose) sendReadiness()
    }
  }

  /** From any thread (CD37): the glue's preview view attached to a window, or detached. */
  fun viewfinder(shown: Boolean) {
    viewfinder = shown
    guarded.schedule(0) { noticeCapture() }
  }

  /**
   * Carry 12: a JS line, posted. A whole JS number prints as `3`, not `3.0`; a fraction is kept and
   * written to tenths like every native number. An unknown level is `info`.
   */
  fun log(level: String, kind: String, fields: Map<String, Any?>) {
    val kept = if (level in LEVELS) level else "info"
    engine.log(RecordEntry(kind, fields.map { (key, value) -> key to whole(value) }, kept))
  }

  fun current(): Map<String, Any?> = current

  fun tail(): List<String> = record.lastLines()

  private fun notice() {
    noticePair()
    noticeCapture()
  }

  /** A new pairing: its PAIRING-scope failures may be healed (CD11), and it hears the platform's readiness at once. */
  private fun noticePair() {
    val request = (engine.phase as? Phase.Pairing)?.pairing?.request ?: return
    if (request === noticed) return
    noticed = request
    sticky.pairAccepted()
    sendReadiness()
  }

  /** Each change is a record line too: the post-match record shows when the phone was ready (AGENTS §11). */
  private fun sendReadiness() {
    sent = readiness
    val fields = listOf("camera" to readiness.cameraFrames, "sound" to readiness.sound, "held" to readiness.held, "side" to readiness.side)
    engine.log(RecordEntry("readiness", fields))
    engine.send(Input.ReadinessChanged(readiness))
  }

  /** CD37: on a change of [captureWanted], or of the pairing it is wanted for (a re-pair over a shown viewfinder). */
  private fun noticeCapture() {
    val phase = engine.phase
    val wanted = phase.holdsBroadcast || (phase is Phase.Paired && viewfinder)
    val request = if (wanted) phase.pairing?.request else null
    if (wanted == captureWanted && request === capturedFor) return
    captureWanted = wanted
    capturedFor = request
    platform.capture(wanted, phase.pairing?.request)
  }

  private fun route(command: Command) {
    pollers.onCommand(command)
    when (command) {
      is Command.FetchPlaylist ->
        platform.http(HttpRequests.playlist(command)) { outcome ->
          checkedAtMs = clock.wallMs()
          report(HttpAnswers.playlist(command.requestId, outcome))
        }
      is Command.PostHeartbeat -> beat(command)
      is Command.FetchCode -> platform.http(HttpRequests.code(command)) { report(HttpAnswers.code(command.requestId, it, command.environment)) }
      is Command.PostStart -> platform.http(HttpRequests.start(command)) { report(HttpAnswers.start(command.requestId, it)) }
      is Command.WriteStopped -> stored("write") { pairings.write(command.record) }
      is Command.DeleteStopped -> stored("delete") { pairings.delete(command.code, command.slot) }
      else -> executed(command)
    }
  }

  /** The environment is read here, on the scheduler thread, for the answer that comes back on any thread. */
  private fun beat(command: Command.PostHeartbeat) {
    val env = engine.phase.pairing?.request?.environment ?: Environment.STAGING
    platform.http(HttpRequests.heartbeat(command)) { report(HttpAnswers.heartbeat(command.beatId, it, env)) }
  }

  /** A refused write is a record line, never silent (AGENTS §13, class 3), and never stops the `End` behind it. */
  private fun stored(op: String, write: () -> Unit) {
    try {
      write()
    } catch (failure: Exception) {
      engine.log(RecordEntry("store-failed", listOf("op" to op, "error" to failure.javaClass.simpleName)))
    }
  }

  /** CD11: a permanent failure is sticky, never retried; anything else is plan B's `command-failed`. */
  private fun executed(command: Command) {
    try {
      platform.execute(command)
    } catch (failure: Throwable) {
      if (!Failures.permanent(failure)) throw failure
      sticky.fail(Failures.describe(failure), engine.phase.attemptInHand, Scope.PROCESS)
    }
  }

  private fun published(snapshot: Snapshot) {
    val phase = engine.phase
    ticks.observe(clock.monotonicMs(), wakeHeld = phase is Phase.Paired || phase.holdsBroadcast)?.let(engine::log)
    val wire = wire(snapshot, platform.facts().copy(deliveryCheckedAtMs = checkedAtMs))
    language = snapshot.language
    current = wire
    platform.snapshot(wire)
  }

  private fun wire(snapshot: Snapshot, facts: PlatformFacts): Map<String, Any?> =
    SnapshotWire.of(snapshot, facts, RecordCounters(record.sinkFailures, record.reentrantDropped))

  /** The Frames poller's read, with CD33's gap line. Scheduler thread. */
  private fun frames(attemptId: Int): FrameCount? {
    val count = platform.frames(attemptId) ?: return null
    gaps.read(attemptId, count.video, clock.monotonicMs(), engine.phase is Phase.OnAir)?.let(engine::log)
    return count
  }

  /** Whatever reached the task boundary (carry 15): recorded, and sticky when permanent (CD11). */
  private fun failed(t: Throwable) {
    engine.log(RecordEntry("engine-error", listOf("message" to Failures.describe(t))))
    if (Failures.permanent(t)) sticky.fail(Failures.describe(t), engine.phase.attemptInHand, Scope.PROCESS)
  }

  private fun whole(value: Any?): Any? = if (value is Double && value % 1.0 == 0.0 && abs(value) <= MAX_EXACT) value.toLong() else value

  companion object {
    private val LEVELS = setOf("debug", "info", "warn", "error")

    /** 2^53: every whole Double up to it is exact. */
    private const val MAX_EXACT = 9_007_199_254_740_992.0

    @Volatile private var instance: BridgeCore? = null

    /** One engine per process (carry 18). A JS reload makes a new module over this same core (CD32). */
    fun shared(factory: () -> BridgeCore): BridgeCore = instance ?: synchronized(this) { instance ?: factory().also { instance = it } }

    /** Tests only: the next [shared] builds afresh. */
    internal fun resetShared() {
      synchronized(this) { instance = null }
    }
  }
}
```

Check before compiling, and fix the call, never the rule: `Phase.pairing` and `Phase.holdsBroadcast` are Task 5's extensions; `Phase.Idle()` takes defaults for every field; `Readiness.sound` is Task 4's; `RecordEntry` has its `level` from Task 10; `CodeAnswer`'s environment comes with the command (`FetchCode.environment`, Task 5). `NaN % 1.0` is `NaN`, so a non-finite number stays a `Double` and the record masks it (CD6).

The test doubles:

```kotlin
package com.seazn.capture.engine.adapter

/** App-private storage in memory. [refuseWrites] makes every write throw, as a full disk would. */
class MemoryStore : PrivateStore {
  val files = mutableMapOf<String, String>()
  var refuseWrites = false

  override fun read(name: String): String? = files[name]

  override fun write(name: String, text: String) {
    if (refuseWrites) throw java.io.IOException("disk full")
    files[name] = text
  }

  override fun delete(name: String) {
    files.remove(name)
  }
}

```kotlin
package com.seazn.capture.engine.adapter

import com.seazn.capture.engine.core.Command
import com.seazn.capture.engine.core.Configs
import com.seazn.capture.engine.core.DropReason
import com.seazn.capture.engine.core.Input
import com.seazn.capture.engine.core.LinkCounters
import com.seazn.capture.engine.core.PairRequest
import com.seazn.capture.engine.core.attemptInHand

/** Records every call, answers the server from [PairWire], and plays a phone that grants and connects. */
class RecordingPlatform : Platform {
  lateinit var core: BridgeCore
  val lines = mutableListOf<String>()
  val snapshots = mutableListOf<Map<String, Any?>>()
  val executed = mutableListOf<Command>()
  val http = mutableListOf<HttpRequest>()
  val captures = mutableListOf<Boolean>()
  val captureRequests = mutableListOf<PairRequest?>()
  val events = mutableListOf<String>()
  var grant = true

  /** False: the permission request is never answered, as when there is no activity to ask from. */
  var ask = true
  var throwOnConnect: Throwable? = null
  var throwOnFactsOnce: Throwable? = null
  var frozen = false
  var answer: (HttpRequest) -> HttpOutcome = PairWire::answer
  private var video = 0L
  private var audio = 0L
  private var connected: Int? = null

  override fun execute(command: Command) {
    executed += command
    when (command) {
      Command.AskPermissions -> if (ask) core.report(Input.PermissionsAnswered(grant))
      is Command.Connect -> {
        throwOnConnect?.let { throw it }
        connected = command.attemptId
        core.report(Input.Connected(command.attemptId))
      }
      else -> Unit
    }
  }

  override fun http(request: HttpRequest, answer: (HttpOutcome) -> Unit) {
    http += request
    answer(this.answer(request))
  }

  override fun capture(wanted: Boolean, request: PairRequest?) {
    captures += wanted
    captureRequests += request
  }

  override fun frames(attemptId: Int): FrameCount? {
    if (attemptId != connected) return null
    if (!frozen) {
      video += 15
      audio += 23
    }
    return FrameCount(video, audio)
  }

  override fun link(attemptId: Int): LinkCounters? = if (attemptId == connected) LinkCounters(1_000, 10, 0, 0, 0, 40, 120, 3_000_000) else null

  override fun facts(): PlatformFacts {
    throwOnFactsOnce?.let {
      throwOnFactsOnce = null
      throw it
    }
    return PlatformFacts(audioLevel = 0.5)
  }

  override fun snapshot(wire: Map<String, Any?>) {
    snapshots += wire
    events += "snapshot"
  }

  override fun recordLine(line: String) {
    lines += line
  }

  override fun acked(seq: Int) {
    events += "ack:$seq"
  }

  fun dropCurrent() = core.report(Input.Dropped(connected!!, DropReason.ENDPOINT_CLOSED, "cut"))

  fun beats() = http.filter { it.url.endsWith("/beat") }
}
```

`PairWire` holds the pair wire (moved from `PairMappingTest`) and the server's made-up answers, built from `Configs`' values with `Json.obj`, so no credential is typed twice:

```kotlin
package com.seazn.capture.engine.adapter

import com.seazn.capture.engine.core.Configs
import com.seazn.capture.engine.core.Json
import com.seazn.capture.engine.core.JsonObject

object PairWire {
  const val ORIGIN = "https://stg.seazn.club/api/capture/codes/fx-42"

  fun valid(): Map<String, Any?> =
    mapOf(
      "kind" to "pair",
      "code" to "fx-42",
      "slot" to 1.0,
      "token" to Configs.TOKEN,
      "codeUrl" to ORIGIN,
      "heartbeatUrl" to "$ORIGIN/beat",
      "startUrl" to "$ORIGIN/start",
      "language" to "fr",
      "automatic" to false,
      "claim" to "new",
      "environment" to "staging",
    )

  private val waiting =
    listOf(
      "label" to "Example Town v Sample CC",
      "venueTimezone" to "Europe/London",
      "scheduledStart" to null,
      "autoAllowed" to true,
      "destinationName" to "YouTube · Example Town CC",
      "overlayUrl" to null,
      "pollSeconds" to 10,
    )

  /** A beat's answer: [state] with the waiting fields, and [sid] when one is named. */
  fun beat(state: String = "waiting", sid: String? = null, endReason: String? = null): String =
    Json.obj(listOf("state" to state, "sid" to sid, "endReason" to endReason) + waiting)

  /** GET code's session shape for sess_42, SRT preferred, on the staging ingest host. */
  val SESSION: String =
    Json.obj(
      listOf(
        "state" to "warming",
        "code" to "fx-42",
        "sid" to "sess_42",
        "cred" to JsonObject(listOf(
          "srt" to JsonObject(listOf("url" to "srt://live.stg.seazn.club:778", "streamId" to Configs.STREAM_ID, "passphrase" to Configs.PASSPHRASE, "latencyMs" to 2_000)),
          "rtmps" to JsonObject(listOf("url" to "rtmps://live.stg.seazn.club:443/live/", "streamKey" to Configs.STREAM_KEY)),
        )),
        "preferred" to "srt",
        "playbackUrl" to Configs.PLAYBACK_URL,
        "holdWindowSeconds" to JsonObject(listOf("srt" to 183, "rtmps" to 180)),
        "maxDurationMinutes" to 300,
        "warmingDeadline" to 1_790_000_600L,
        "scoreUpdates" to "realtime",
      ) + waiting,
    )

  /** The default server: beats wait, the code is open, a start succeeds, a playlist has a variant. */
  fun answer(request: HttpRequest): HttpOutcome =
    when {
      request.url.endsWith("/beat") -> HttpOutcome.Answered(200, beat())
      request.url.endsWith("/start") -> HttpOutcome.Answered(200, """{"sid":"sess_42"}""")
      request.url.startsWith("$ORIGIN?") -> HttpOutcome.Answered(200, SESSION)
      else -> HttpOutcome.Answered(200, "#EXTM3U\n#EXT-X-STREAM-INF:BANDWIDTH=1\nv.m3u8")
    }
}

    scheduler.advanceBy(Engine.TICK_MS)
    assertTrue(lines().any { it.getString("kind") == "engine-error" && "StackOverflowError" in it.getString("message") })
    val before = platform.snapshots.size
    scheduler.advanceBy(Engine.TICK_MS * 4)
    assertEquals(before + 4, platform.snapshots.size, "every later tick still publishes")
  }

  @Test
  fun `G0-d the code is asked with its slot and this phone's id`() {
    live()
    val asked = platform.http.single { it.url.startsWith("${PairWire.ORIGIN}?") }
    assertEquals("${PairWire.ORIGIN}?slot=1&phone=${Configs.PHONE_ID}", asked.url)
  }

  @Test
  fun `A17 the operator's Stop is stored before the end, and rides the next pairing's first beat`() {
    live()
    core.send(mapOf("kind" to "stop"))
    scheduler.advanceBy(0)
    assertTrue("sess_42" in store.files.getValue(PairingStore.STOPPED))
    core.send(mapOf("kind" to "reset"))
    scheduler.advanceBy(0)
    platform.http.clear()
    pair()
    assertEquals("sess_42", JSONObject(platform.beats().first().body!!).getString("stopped"))
  }

  @Test
  fun `a refused write is a record line, and the end still happens`() {
    live()
    store.refuseWrites = true
    core.send(mapOf("kind" to "stop"))
    scheduler.advanceBy(0)
    assertEquals("ended", state())
    assertTrue(lines().any { it.getString("kind") == "store-failed" && it.getString("op") == "write" })
  }

  @Test
  fun `the phone id is made once and kept across engines over the same storage`() {
    live()
    val again = RecordingPlatform()
    val second = build(again)
    second.start()
    pair(second)
    val ids = (platform.beats() + again.beats()).map { JSONObject(it.body!!).getString("phone") }.toSet()
    assertEquals(setOf(Configs.PHONE_ID), ids)
  }

  @Test
  fun `carry 12 a forwarded JS line is written through the scheduler, its level kept and a level field renamed`() {
    core.start()
    core.log("warn", "intent.stop", mapOf("level" to "x", "count" to 3.0, "ms" to 2.25))
    assertTrue(platform.lines.none { "intent.stop" in it }, "not written before the scheduler runs it")
    scheduler.advanceBy(0)
    val line = JSONObject(platform.lines.single { "intent.stop" in it })
    assertEquals("warn", line.getString("level"))
    // Renamed, and masked: a field called `level` is on no allow-list (Task 10).
    assertEquals("***", line.getString("field_level"))
    // P6: `get`, not `getInt`, which would coerce 3.0 and let the mutant through.
    assertEquals(3, line.get("count"))
    // Decimal.tenths: Math.round(2.25 × 10) = Math.round(22.5) = 23, so 2.3.
    assertEquals(2.3, line.getDouble("ms"), "a fraction is written to tenths, like every native number")
  }

  @Test
  fun `CD33 a tick that comes late while paired is recorded with its gap`() {
    var stall = false
    val slow =
      object : Scheduler {
        override fun schedule(delayMs: Long, task: () -> Unit): Cancellable =
          scheduler.schedule(if (stall && delayMs == Engine.TICK_MS) 2_000 else delayMs, task)
      }
    val late = RecordingPlatform()
    val stalled = build(late, MemoryStore(), slow)
    stalled.start()
    stalled.send(PairWire.valid())
    scheduler.advanceBy(Engine.TICK_MS)
    stall = true
    // The tick already due runs on time and schedules the next 2 000 ms out: one gap of 2 000 ms.
    scheduler.advanceBy(Engine.TICK_MS + 2_000)
    assertEquals(listOf(2_000L), lines(late).filter { it.getString("kind") == "tick-late" }.map { it.getLong("gapMs") })
  }

  @Test
  fun `CD33 video that stops moving while live is one frames-gap line with its length`() {
    live()
    // Reads run every 500 ms from the Connected at 0; the last one at 1 500 moved the count.
    platform.frozen = true
    scheduler.advanceBy(1_500)
    platform.frozen = false
    scheduler.advanceBy(500)
    // Last moved at 1 500, moved again at 3 500: 2 000 ms.
    val gap = lines().single { it.getString("kind") == "frames-gap" }
    assertEquals(2_000L, gap.getLong("gapMs"))
  }

  @Test
  fun `carry 18 one engine per process`() {
    BridgeCore.resetShared()
    var built = 0
    val first = BridgeCore.shared { built += 1; core }
    val second = BridgeCore.shared { built += 1; core }
    assertSame(first, second)
    assertEquals(1, built)
  }
}

(4) Another mode, orientation or language: the notification's language is the pairing's, then `setLanguage`'s (P3).

### Task 21: The JVM host

Carry 1 and CD8. A small program runs `BridgeCore` with a scripted platform and a scripted Seazn server, and speaks NDJSON on stdin and stdout. This is how the JS contract kit (Task 23) reaches the real core through the real mapping, with no phone. The amendment widens the script: the platform grants permissions and reports a ready phone, and the server answers beats, `GET code` and `POST start`, each replaceable from stdin, so the kit can drive an organiser's Go live, a refusal or an end without a network.

Pre-flight **P7** is folded: the JVM host runs a real 500 ms tick, so a snapshot may follow the ack; `ProtocolTest` asserts the refused pair's snapshot is before the ack, and no longer that the ack is last.

**Files:**

- Modify: `modules/capture-engine/android/core/settings.gradle.kts`: add `include("host")`, and update the header comment, which says the core is consumed through `includeBuild` (CD2 reverses that)
- Create: `modules/capture-engine/android/core/host/build.gradle.kts`, and under `host/src/main/kotlin/com/seazn/capture/engine/host/`: `Main.kt`, `Host.kt`, `ScriptedPlatform.kt`, `ScriptedServer.kt`, `Protocol.kt`, `ExecutorScheduler.kt`
- Create: `host/src/test/kotlin/com/seazn/capture/engine/host/ProtocolTest.kt`, `ScriptedServerTest.kt`

**Interfaces:**

- **stdin**, one JSON object a line:
  - `{"op":"send","seq":n,"intent":{…}}`;
  - `{"op":"log","level":"info","kind":"x","fields":{…}}`;
  - `{"op":"script","path":"beat"|"code"|"start","status":n,"body":{…}}`: from now on, that path is answered with `status` and `body`;
  - `{"op":"readiness","camera":bool,"audioPeak":n,"pose":"left"|"right"|"not-held"|"no-sensor"}`, every field optional;
  - `{"op":"exit"}`.
- **stdout**, one JSON object a line:
  - `{"ev":"ready","current":{…},"tail":[…]}`, first;
  - then `{"ev":"snapshot","body":{…}}`, `{"ev":"record","line":"…"}`, `{"ev":"request","path":"beat"|"code"|"start","body":…}` and `{"ev":"ack","seq":n}`.
- **The ack (CD8).** `BridgeCore.send` posts `platform.acked(seq)` after the input's own tasks (Task 20), and the host's platform writes it as `{"ev":"ack","seq":n}`. The scheduler runs equal delays in the order they were posted (a `ScheduledThreadPoolExecutor` breaks ties by submission order), so the ack is written after every snapshot and record line that input caused. An intent the machine ignores is acked too, so the kit never waits on a timeout.
- **`request` events** carry the body the engine sent (a beat's JSON, or `{phone}` for a start), never the URL or the Bearer, so the kit can assert the claim, `stopped` and `notReady` without a network and without a secret on stdout. The made-up token is still a secret by rule: the host never writes it.
- Nothing else is written to stdout. Diagnostics go to stderr.

package com.seazn.capture.engine.host

import kotlin.test.Test
import kotlin.test.assertEquals
import kotlin.test.assertFalse
import kotlin.test.assertTrue
import org.json.JSONObject

class ProtocolTest {
  @Test
  fun `numbers cross as doubles, as they do through Expo`() {
    val wire = Protocol.toWire(JSONObject("""{"kind":"pair","slot":2,"nested":{"n":2000},"claim":null}"""))
    assertEquals(2.0, wire["slot"])
    assertEquals(2000.0, (wire["nested"] as Map<*, *>)["n"])
    assertEquals(null, wire["claim"])
    assertTrue(wire.containsKey("claim"))
  }

  @Test
  fun `an event is one line`() {
    val line = Protocol.encode("record", mapOf("line" to "{\"a\":1}\n"))
    assertFalse('\n' in line)
    assertEquals("{\"a\":1}\n", JSONObject(line).getString("line"))
  }

  @Test
  fun `CD8 P7 the refused pair's snapshot is written before that intent's ack`() {
    val out = mutableListOf<String>()
    val executor = ExecutorScheduler()
    val host = Host(executor) { synchronized(out) { out += it } }
    host.handle("""{"op":"send","seq":1,"intent":{"kind":"pair"}}""")
    executor.drain()
    val events = synchronized(out) { out.map(::JSONObject) }
    val ack = events.indexOfFirst { it.getString("ev") == "ack" }
    val ended = events.indexOfFirst { it.getString("ev") == "snapshot" && it.getJSONObject("body").getJSONObject("state").getString("kind") == "ended" }
    assertTrue(ended in 0 until ack, "the refused pair's ended snapshot comes before its ack")
    executor.shutdown()
  }

  @Test
  fun `no line the host writes carries the made-up token or a URL`() {
    val out = mutableListOf<String>()
    val executor = ExecutorScheduler()
    val host = Host(executor) { synchronized(out) { out += it } }
    host.handle("""{"op":"send","seq":1,"intent":${ScriptedServer.PAIR}}""")
    host.handle("""{"op":"send","seq":2,"intent":{"kind":"start"}}""")
    executor.drain()
    val all = synchronized(out) { out.joinToString("\n") }
    assertFalse(ScriptedServer.TOKEN in all)
    assertFalse("https://" in all.substringAfter("\"ev\":\"request\"", ""), "a request event carries the body only")
    executor.shutdown()
  }
}

`Host(scheduler, write)` is `Main`'s logic without stdin and stdout, so it is testable. `ExecutorScheduler.drain()` is a test helper: it schedules a marker task with delay 0 and waits for it, repeating until no task was posted meanwhile. A pair with no fields is refused at once, so its snapshot is certain. The JVM scheduler's tie order is what this test adds over Task 20's, which ran on `FakeScheduler`.

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement.**
  - **`ExecutorScheduler`** wraps one `ScheduledExecutorService` thread named `capture-engine`. Its `Cancellable` cancels the future.
  - **The clock** is `System.nanoTime() / 1_000_000` for monotonic time and `System.currentTimeMillis()` for wall time.
  - **`ScriptedServer`**, below: made-up values only, on the staging hosts, so the real `Bodies` and `Hosts` rules accept them.
  - **`ScriptedPlatform`**:
    - `AskPermissions` is answered `PermissionsAnswered(true)`; `Hold`, `Release`, `Orient`, `StopBroadcast` and `Record` are written to stderr and otherwise ignored.
    - It answers `Connect` with `core.report(signals.connected(id))` 100 ms later, on its own single-thread executor. From then on, `frames(id)` returns counts that grow by 15 video and 23 audio every 500 ms.
    - `Disconnect`, `Rebuild`, `StartNewSession`, `StopBroadcast` and `End` stop the counting, and a `Rebuild` or `StartNewSession` connects its `next` the same way.
    - `http` asks `ScriptedServer.answer`, writes `{"ev":"request","path":…,"body":…}` for a beat, code or start request (the body parsed back to an object, or null), and answers on its own executor.
    - `capture(wanted, request)` writes a stderr line; it never fails.
    - Its facts are `PlatformFacts(audioLevel = 0.5, survivesBackground = true)`.
    - `snapshot` and `recordLine` write events to stdout, under a lock.
  - **`Host(scheduler, write: (String) -> Unit)`** builds the core over the scheduler, a `ScriptedPlatform` that writes through `write`, an in-memory `PrivateStore` and `newId = { "host-phone" }`; it reports `Network(true)`, calls `core.readiness(cameraFrames = true, audioPeak = 0.5, pose = Pose.Held(Side.LEFT))` and `start()`. `handle(line)` parses one stdin line: `send` calls `core.send(Protocol.toWire(intent))` with the line's `seq` put into the intent map; `log` calls `core.log`; `script` calls `server.script`; `readiness` calls `core.readiness` with the fields given; a line that does not parse goes to stderr and is skipped. `ScriptedPlatform.acked(seq)` writes `Protocol.encode("ack", mapOf("seq" to seq))`.
  - **`Main`** builds a `Host` over an `ExecutorScheduler`, writing to stdout under a lock. It writes `ready` with `current()` and `tail()`, then feeds stdin to `handle` line by line until `exit` or EOF. On exit it shuts the executors down and exits 0.

```kotlin
package com.seazn.capture.engine.host

import com.seazn.capture.engine.adapter.HttpOutcome
import com.seazn.capture.engine.adapter.HttpRequest
import org.json.JSONObject

/** The host's Seazn: made-up answers on the staging hosts, each path replaceable by a script line. */
class ScriptedServer {
  private val answers =
    mutableMapOf(
      "beat" to (200 to WAITING),
      "code" to (200 to SESSION),
      "start" to (200 to JSONObject().put("sid", "sess_host")),
    )

  @Synchronized
  fun script(path: String, status: Int, body: JSONObject) {
    require(path in answers) { "unknown path $path" }
    answers[path] = status to body
  }

  /** The path a request is for, or null for anything that is not Seazn's (a playlist). */
  fun path(request: HttpRequest): String? =
    when {
      request.url.endsWith("/beat") -> "beat"
      request.url.endsWith("/start") -> "start"
      request.url.startsWith("$ORIGIN?") -> "code"
      else -> null
    }

  @Synchronized
  fun answer(request: HttpRequest): HttpOutcome {
    val (status, body) = answers[path(request) ?: return HttpOutcome.Failed("scripted host: no network")]!!
    return HttpOutcome.Answered(status, body.toString())
  }

  companion object {
    const val ORIGIN = "https://stg.seazn.club/api/capture/codes/host-code"
    const val TOKEN = "tok-host-0000000000000000"

    /** The pair intent the kit sends: made-up, staging, slot 0. */
    val PAIR: String =
      JSONObject()
        .put("kind", "pair").put("code", "host-code").put("slot", 0).put("token", TOKEN)
        .put("codeUrl", ORIGIN).put("heartbeatUrl", "$ORIGIN/beat").put("startUrl", "$ORIGIN/start")
        .put("language", "en").put("automatic", true).put("claim", "new").put("environment", "staging")
        .toString()

    private fun waiting(state: String) =
      JSONObject()
        .put("state", state).put("label", "Host v Script").put("venueTimezone", "Europe/London")
        .put("scheduledStart", JSONObject.NULL).put("autoAllowed", true).put("destinationName", "YouTube · Host")
        .put("overlayUrl", JSONObject.NULL).put("pollSeconds", 10)

    val WAITING: JSONObject = waiting("waiting")

    val SESSION: JSONObject =
      waiting("warming")
        .put("code", "host-code").put("sid", "sess_host").put("preferred", "srt")
        .put("cred", JSONObject()
          .put("srt", JSONObject().put("url", "srt://live.stg.seazn.club:778").put("streamId", "host-stream-id").put("passphrase", "host-passphrase-0").put("latencyMs", 2000))

## Batch C4b — the JS stable code, the switch, and identity

The suite is `pnpm check` and `pnpm i18n:release-check`. Task 22 adds the QR v2 and waiting-field parsers beside today's; Task 23 switches the app to the paired port in one commit, with the fake engine's paired phase and the kit's paired scenarios, and deletes `StreamSession` and the descriptor path; Task 24 adds the identity and reopen rules. The fake engine stays wired in production until Task 32.

### Task 22: The JS domain for the stable code — the QR, the waiting fields and the code port

Amendment §3, _The JS_, first bullet, and _Who reads what_: JS parses the QR and the waiting fields, and never sees `cred`. Everything here is new and pure, or a port with a fake. Nothing is wired yet: Task 23 is the switch, and it wires the code port into `createNativePorts` (recurring failure class 1; Task 23's Step 9 greps for it). Until then the new modules are reached only by their tests, which this task says out loud so the reviewer does not read it as an inert seam.

**Files:**

- Create: `src/domain/credentials/streamCode.ts`, `src/domain/credentials/streamCode.test.ts`
- Create: `src/domain/credentials/waitingFields.ts`, `src/domain/credentials/waitingFields.test.ts`
- Create: `modules/capture-engine/src/waitingVectors.test.ts` (reads Task 15's `waiting-vectors.json`)
- Create: `src/services/httpAsk.ts`, `src/services/httpAsk.test.ts` (the deadline race and `parseRetryAfter`, moved out of `fetchDescriptorPort.ts`, which Task 23 deletes)
- Modify: `src/services/fetchDescriptorPort.ts` (imports the four moved names from `httpAsk`), `src/services/fetchDescriptorPort.test.ts` (its import block, and its two `parseRetryAfter` tests move to `httpAsk.test.ts`)
- Create: `src/services/codePort.ts`, `src/services/fetchCodePort.ts`, `src/services/fetchCodePort.test.ts`, `src/services/fakeCodePort.ts`, `src/services/fakeCodePort.test.ts`

Do not touch: `parseCaptureQr.ts`, `parseDescriptor.ts`, `savedCode.ts`, `recognise.ts` or any hook. They move in Task 23, in one switch, so that every commit between here and there is green.

**Interfaces:**

- Consumes `wire.ts` (`isRecord`, `readString`, `readInteger`, `readEpochSeconds`, `httpsHost`, `WireError`), `Result`, `Logger`, `seaznHosts`, and Task 15's `modules/capture-engine/src/wire/waiting-vectors.json`.
- Produces:
  - `type StreamCode = { code: string; slot: number; token: string; expiresAt: Date | null }`, `parseStreamCode(input: unknown): Result<StreamCode, WireError>`, `parseStreamCodeText(text: string)`;
  - `type WaitingFields = { code, label, venueTimezone, scheduledStart: Date | null, autoAllowed, destinationName: string | null, overlayUrl: string | null, pollSeconds, heartbeatUrl, startUrl }`, `parseWaitingFields(input: unknown, host: string): WaitingFields | null`, `CODE_STATES`, `waitingToWire(fields)`;
  - `type CodeError = invalid | not-found | ended | offline | rate-limited{retryAfterS}` (spec: "`DescriptorError` keeps `ended`, read as not valid"; it is renamed with the port it belongs to);
  - `interface CodePort { check(code: StreamCode): Promise<Result<WaitingFields, CodeError>>; codeUrl(code: string): string }`;
  - `createFetchCodePort({ origin, fetch, logger, timeoutMs?, now? })`, `codeUrl(origin, code)`, `CODE_TIMEOUT_MS = 8000`;
  - `createFakeCodePort(origin?)`, `sampleWaiting(overrides?)`, `SAMPLE_CODE = 'fx-42'`;
  - `httpAsk.ts`: `type FetchResponse`, `type FetchLike`, `parseRetryAfter(value, nowMs)`, `withDeadline(work, ms, onLate, onThrow)`.

**The rules this task builds.**

- **QR v2 is `{ v:2, code, slot, tok, exp? }`** (A1, _Contract shapes_). `exp` is optional; `null` reads as absent. A code with no `code` is refused, so a pre-amendment v2 (with `sid` and `cred`) reads as `missing-field code`, never half-parsed. Any `cred` a mis-issued code carries is ignored and never kept in the parsed value.
- **The waiting fields are read from any 200**, `waiting` or session-shaped (round 5: the session shape carries them). JS reads `code`, `label`, `venueTimezone`, `scheduledStart`, `autoAllowed`, `destinationName`, `overlayUrl`, `pollSeconds`, `heartbeatUrl` and `startUrl`, and nothing else; `cred` is never read, and the type has no place for it.
- **The Seazn-host rule** is the existing one (ruling 6): `heartbeatUrl` and `startUrl` must sit on the build's exact host, or the answer is refused whole, because the Bearer would go there; a foreign `overlayUrl` is dropped and the rest kept, as Kotlin does. Task 15's vector file pins both readers; its `jsOnly` rows cover the three fields only JS keeps.
- **The scan's `GET code` sends `?slot=<n>` and never `?phone=`** (round 5; G0-d: "phone from native only, never JS's scan fetch"). Bearer `tok`, `Cache-Control: no-store`.
- **The outcome table** (amendment §2): 200 → the waiting fields; 401 → `invalid`; 404 → `not-found`; 410 → `ended` (a server fault at a scan, read as not valid); 429 → `rate-limited` with Retry-After; anything else, a network failure or 8 s with no whole answer → `offline`. A 200 whose `code` is not the code asked for is `invalid` (`code-mismatch`), the same guard D3 kept for the sid.

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement** `src/domain/credentials/streamCode.ts`:

```ts
import { type Result, err, ok } from '@/domain/Result';
import {
  isRecord,
  readEpochSeconds,
  readInteger,
  readString,
  type WireError,
} from '@/domain/credentials/wire';

/**
 * capture-qr v2 after the stable code (amendment A1): a code and its camera
 * position, with no credentials and no session. The phone pairs once per code,
 * and the server starts and stops each broadcast.
 */
export type StreamCode = {
  readonly code: string;
  readonly slot: number;
  /** The code's Bearer for `GET code`, beats and `POST start`. A secret: never log it. */
  readonly token: string;
  /** The QR's optional `exp`; null when the printed code carries none. */
  readonly expiresAt: Date | null;
};

type Read<T> = Result<T, WireError>;

const VERSION = 2;

export function parseStreamCodeText(text: string): Read<StreamCode> {
  let data: unknown;
  try {
    data = JSON.parse(text);
  } catch {
    return err({ kind: 'not-an-object' });
  }
  return parseStreamCode(data);
}

/** The anti-corruption layer for the QR (AGENTS §4): the wire shape stops here. */
export function parseStreamCode(input: unknown): Read<StreamCode> {
  if (!isRecord(input)) return err({ kind: 'not-an-object' });
  if (input.v !== VERSION) {
    return err({
      kind: 'unsupported-version',
      found: typeof input.v === 'number' ? input.v : null,
    });
  }
  const code = readString(input, 'code');
  if (!code.ok) return code;
  const slot = readInteger(input, 'slot', 0);
  if (!slot.ok) return slot;
  const token = readString(input, 'tok');
  if (!token.ok) return token;
  const expiresAt =
    input.exp === undefined || input.exp === null ? ok(null) : readEpochSeconds(input, 'exp');
  if (!expiresAt.ok) return expiresAt;
  return ok({ code: code.value, slot: slot.value, token: token.value, expiresAt: expiresAt.value });
}
```

- [ ] **Step 5: Implement** `src/domain/credentials/waitingFields.ts`:

```ts
import { httpsHost, isRecord } from '@/domain/credentials/wire';

/**
 * What a stream code says while it waits for a Go live (amendment, Contract
 * shapes): read by JS at the scan, saved with the code, and read again by
 * native on every beat. Publish credentials are never part of it (A1, A5).
 */
export type WaitingFields = {
  readonly code: string;
  readonly label: string;
  readonly venueTimezone: string;
  readonly scheduledStart: Date | null;
  readonly autoAllowed: boolean;
  readonly destinationName: string | null;
  readonly overlayUrl: string | null;
  readonly pollSeconds: number;
  readonly heartbeatUrl: string;
  readonly startUrl: string;
};

/** Why a scanned code could not be checked. `ended` (a 410 at a scan) reads as not valid. */
export type CodeError =
  | { readonly kind: 'invalid' }
  | { readonly kind: 'not-found' }
  | { readonly kind: 'ended' }
  | { readonly kind: 'offline' }
  | { readonly kind: 'rate-limited'; readonly retryAfterS: number };

/** The states a 200 from `GET code` may carry; each carries the waiting fields (round 5). */
export const CODE_STATES = ['waiting', 'warming', 'live', 'ending', 'completed', 'failed'] as const;

const isText = (value: unknown): value is string => typeof value === 'string';
const isWhole = (value: unknown): value is number =>
  typeof value === 'number' && Number.isInteger(value);
/** Ruling 6: exactly the build's host, https only; an empty host trusts nothing. */
const onHost = (url: unknown, host: string): url is string =>
  isText(url) && host !== '' && httpsHost(url) === host;

/**
 * The waiting fields, or null when the answer cannot be trusted whole: a
 * missing field, or a beat or start URL off the build's host (its Bearer
 * would go there). A foreign overlay is dropped and the rest kept, as
 * Bodies.waiting does in Kotlin; Task 15's vectors pin both.
 */
export function parseWaitingFields(input: unknown, host: string): WaitingFields | null {
  if (!isRecord(input)) return null;
  const { code, label, venueTimezone, autoAllowed, pollSeconds, heartbeatUrl, startUrl } = input;
  if (!isText(code) || code === '' || !isText(label) || !isText(venueTimezone)) return null;
  if (typeof autoAllowed !== 'boolean' || !isWhole(pollSeconds)) return null;
  if (!onHost(heartbeatUrl, host) || !onHost(startUrl, host)) return null;
  const { scheduledStart, destinationName, overlayUrl } = input;
  return {
    code,
    label,
    venueTimezone,
    scheduledStart: isWhole(scheduledStart) ? new Date(scheduledStart * 1000) : null,
    autoAllowed,
    destinationName: isText(destinationName) ? destinationName : null,
    overlayUrl: onHost(overlayUrl, host) ? overlayUrl : null,
    pollSeconds,
    heartbeatUrl,
    startUrl,
  };
}

/** The server's own shape, epoch seconds included, so a saved code is read back by the one parser. */
export function waitingToWire(fields: WaitingFields): Record<string, unknown> {
  const { scheduledStart, ...rest } = fields;
  const seconds = scheduledStart === null ? null : Math.floor(scheduledStart.getTime() / 1000);
  return { ...rest, scheduledStart: seconds };
}
```

```ts
/**
 * Races the whole exchange, headers and body, against the clock, so a portal
 * that answers 200 and then trickles nothing is still bounded. The loser is
 * dropped unlogged: a fetch rejecting on the abort is not a second error.
 * Anything the exchange throws is `onThrow()`, so this never rejects.
 */
export function withDeadline<T>(
  work: (signal?: AbortSignal) => Promise<T>,
  ms: number,
  onLate: () => T,
  onThrow: () => T,
): Promise<T> {
  const controller = typeof AbortController === 'function' ? new AbortController() : null;
  let timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined;
  const late = new Promise<T>((resolve) => {
    timer = setTimeout(() => {
      controller?.abort();
      resolve(onLate());
    }, ms);
  });
  const answered = work(controller?.signal).catch(onThrow);
  return Promise.race([answered, late]).finally(() => clearTimeout(timer));
}
```

In `fetchDescriptorPort.test.ts`, import `parseRetryAfter`, `FetchLike` and `FetchResponse` from `@/services/httpAsk`, and move its `describe('parseRetryAfter (D5)')` block (line 399 at `d6931c1`) unchanged into `src/services/httpAsk.test.ts`. const TOKEN = 'tok-9f3c2a7e5b1d4680';
const CODE = { code: 'fx-42', slot: 1, token: TOKEN, expiresAt: null };
const NOW = Date.parse('2026-10-03T13:00:00Z');

const waiting = (overrides: Record<string, unknown> = {}) => ({
  state: 'waiting',
  code: 'fx-42',
  label: 'Example Town v Sample CC',
  venueTimezone: 'Europe/London',
  scheduledStart: null,
  autoAllowed: true,
  destinationName: null,

  pollSeconds: 60,
  heartbeatUrl: 'https://stg.seazn.club/api/capture/codes/fx-42/beat',
  startUrl: 'https://stg.seazn.club/api/capture/codes/fx-42/start',
  ...overrides,
});

const respond = (
  status: number,
  body: unknown = null,
  headers: Record<string, string> = {},
): FetchResponse => ({
  status,
  headers: { get: (name) => headers[name] ?? null },
  json: async () => body,
});

function portOver(fetch: FetchLike, origin = 'https://stg.seazn.club') {
  const record = createRingRecord();
  const calls: Parameters<FetchLike>[] = [];
  const port = createFetchCodePort({
    origin,
    fetch: (url, init) => {
      calls.push([url, init]);
      return fetch(url, init);
    },
    logger: createLogger({ record, now: () => 0 }),
    now: () => NOW,
  });

import type { Result } from '@/domain/Result';
import type { StreamCode } from '@/domain/credentials/streamCode';
import type { CodeError, WaitingFields } from '@/domain/credentials/waitingFields';

/**
 * The server's word on a scanned stream code (amendment §2). Never rejects:
 * every failure is a `CodeError`, so Home always has something true to say.
 */
export interface CodePort {
  check(code: StreamCode): Promise<Result<WaitingFields, CodeError>>;
  /** Where native asks the code again (`GET code`), saved with it (CD36: the build's origin). */
  codeUrl(code: string): string;
}

`src/services/fetchCodePort.ts`:

```ts
import { type Result, err, ok } from '@/domain/Result';
import type { StreamCode } from '@/domain/credentials/streamCode';
import {
  CODE_STATES,
  parseWaitingFields,
  type CodeError,
  type WaitingFields,
} from '@/domain/credentials/waitingFields';
import { httpsHost, isRecord } from '@/domain/credentials/wire';
import type { CodePort } from '@/services/codePort';
import {
  parseRetryAfter,
  withDeadline,
  type FetchLike,
  type FetchResponse,
} from '@/services/httpAsk';
import type { Logger } from '@/services/logger';

/** Bounds a captive portal or a dead cell: after this, "no connection". */
export const CODE_TIMEOUT_MS = 8000;

type Deps = {
  /** The build's origin. Its host is the only one the answer's URLs may name (ruling 6). */
  origin: string;
  fetch: FetchLike;
  logger: Logger;
  timeoutMs?: number;
  now?: () => number;
};

type Refusal = { readonly error: CodeError; readonly status: number; readonly problem?: string };
type Read = { readonly fields: WaitingFields; readonly droppedOverlay: boolean };
/** An answer not yet logged: only the one that wins the deadline race ever is. */
type Verdict = Result<Read, Refusal>;

const OFFLINE: CodeError = { kind: 'offline' };
const INVALID: CodeError = { kind: 'invalid' };

/** Provisional (D2): the web side owns the path; plan D reconciles it with the published schema. */
export function codeUrl(origin: string, code: string): string {
  return `${origin}/api/capture/codes/${encodeURIComponent(code)}`;
}

const refusal = (error: CodeError, status: number, problem?: string): Verdict =>
  err({ error, status, ...(problem ? { problem } : {}) });

export function createFetchCodePort(deps: Deps): CodePort {
  const ms = deps.timeoutMs ?? CODE_TIMEOUT_MS;
  const host = httpsHost(deps.origin) ?? '';
  return {
    check: async (code) => {
      const verdict = await withDeadline(
        (signal) => ask(deps, code, host, signal),
        ms,
        () => refusal(OFFLINE, 0, 'timeout'),
        () => refusal(OFFLINE, 0, 'unexpected'),
      );
      return settle(verdict, deps.logger);
    },
    codeUrl: (code) => codeUrl(deps.origin, code),
  };
}

/** The scan's ask: `?slot=` always, never `?phone=` (G0-d: the phone id is native's). */
async function ask(
  deps: Deps,
  code: StreamCode,
  host: string,
  signal?: AbortSignal,
): Promise<Verdict> {
  const url = `${codeUrl(deps.origin, code.code)}?slot=${code.slot}`;
  const headers = {
    Authorization: `Bearer ${code.token}`,
    'Cache-Control': 'no-store',
    Accept: 'application/json',
  };
  let response: FetchResponse;
  try {
    response = await deps.fetch(url, { method: 'GET', headers, signal });
  } catch {
    return refusal(OFFLINE, 0, 'network');
  }
  return read(response, code.code, host, deps);
}

/** The Home outcome table (amendment §2). */
async function read(
  response: FetchResponse,
  asked: string,
  host: string,
  deps: Deps,
): Promise<Verdict> {
  const { status } = response;
  switch (status) {
    case 200:
      return readFields(await body(response), asked, host);
    case 401:
      return refusal(INVALID, status);
    case 404:
      return refusal({ kind: 'not-found' }, status);
    case 410:
      return refusal({ kind: 'ended' }, status);
    case 429: {
      const retryAfterS = parseRetryAfter(
        response.headers.get('Retry-After'),
        deps.now?.() ?? Date.now(),
      );
      return refusal({ kind: 'rate-limited', retryAfterS }, status);
    }
    default:
      return refusal(OFFLINE, status);
  }
}

function readFields(data: unknown, asked: string, host: string): Verdict {
  if (!isRecord(data) || !CODE_STATES.some((state) => state === data.state)) {
    return refusal(INVALID, 200, 'unparseable');
  }
  const fields = parseWaitingFields(data, host);
  if (fields === null) return refusal(INVALID, 200, 'unparseable');
  if (fields.code !== asked) return refusal(INVALID, 200, 'code-mismatch');
  const droppedOverlay = typeof data.overlayUrl === 'string' && fields.overlayUrl === null;
  return ok({ fields, droppedOverlay });
}

/** A refusal or a dropped overlay is said in the record, never silent (recurring failure class 3). */
function settle(verdict: Verdict, logger: Logger): Result<WaitingFields, CodeError> {
  if (verdict.ok) {
    if (verdict.value.droppedOverlay)
      logger.warn('code.overlay-dropped', { problem: 'foreign-host' });
    return ok(verdict.value.fields);
  }
  const { error, status, problem } = verdict.error;
  logger.warn('code.error', { kind: error.kind, status, ...(problem ? { problem } : {}) });
  return err(error);
}

const body = (response: FetchResponse): Promise<unknown> => response.json().catch(() => null);
```

`src/services/fakeCodePort.ts`:

```ts
import { type Result, ok } from '@/domain/Result';
import type { CodeError, WaitingFields } from '@/domain/credentials/waitingFields';
import type { CodePort } from '@/services/codePort';
import { codeUrl } from '@/services/fetchCodePort';

type Answer = Result<WaitingFields, CodeError>;

export const SAMPLE_CODE = 'fx-42';

/** Made-up waiting fields on the staging host, for the fake and for tests. */
export function sampleWaiting(overrides: Partial<WaitingFields> = {}): WaitingFields {
  const code = overrides.code ?? SAMPLE_CODE;
  return {
    code,
    label: 'Seazn XI v Fake CC',
    venueTimezone: 'Europe/London',
    scheduledStart: null,
    autoAllowed: true,
    destinationName: 'YouTube · Fake CC',
    overlayUrl: 'https://stg.seazn.club/overlay/fixtures/fake-fixture',
    pollSeconds: 60,
    heartbeatUrl: `https://stg.seazn.club/api/capture/codes/${code}/beat`,
    startUrl: `https://stg.seazn.club/api/capture/codes/${code}/start`,
    ...overrides,
  };
}

export type FakeCodePort = CodePort & {
  answer(...results: Answer[]): void;
  hold(): () => void;
  /** Each check's code and slot. The token is never kept, even in a fake. */
  readonly calls: readonly { readonly code: string; readonly slot: number }[];
};

export function createFakeCodePort(origin = 'https://stg.seazn.club'): FakeCodePort {
  const queue: Answer[] = [];
  const calls: { code: string; slot: number }[] = [];
  let gate: Promise<void> | null = null;
  return {
    calls,
    answer: (...results) => {
      queue.push(...results);
    },
    hold: () => {
      let release = () => undefined as void;
      gate = new Promise<void>((resolve) => {
        release = resolve;
      });
      return () => release();
    },
    check: async ({ code, slot }) => {
      calls.push({ code, slot });
      const waiting = gate;
      gate = null;
      if (waiting !== null) await waiting;
      return queue.shift() ?? ok(sampleWaiting({ code }));
    },
    codeUrl: (code) => codeUrl(origin, code),
  };
}
```

```ts
/**
 * CD36: the build's environment, which names its Seazn and ingest hosts. In the
 * domain, not the port, so `services/seaznHosts.ts` may name it (the boundary
 * rule lets services import domain, never engine; review M10).
 */
export type Environment = 'production' | 'staging';

/** The two ways out (C1). Publish credentials themselves are native's (AGENTS §4). */
export type Transport = 'srt' | 'rtmps';

/** How the overlay learns a score (S1 decision 8), echoed in the broadcast. */
export type ScoreUpdates = 'realtime' | 'polled';

/** Who started the broadcast in hand (A2, A10, A16). */
export type Cause = 'organiser' | 'automatic' | 'operator' | 'rejoin';

/** A readiness check native judges (A11), in the order it reports the first that fails. */
export type NotReady = 'camera' | 'sound' | 'network' | 'held';

export const NOT_READY_ORDER: readonly NotReady[] = ['camera', 'sound', 'network', 'held'];

/** Native's verdict on each check; false when unknown. */
export type Readiness = Readonly<Record<NotReady, boolean>>;

export function firstNotReady(ready: Readiness): NotReady | null {
  return NOT_READY_ORDER.find((check) => !ready[check]) ?? null;
}

/** What the snapshot names the pairing by, and its waiting fields (amendment, The engine port). */
export type PairingInfo = {
  readonly code: string;
  readonly slot: number;
  readonly tokenTag: string;
  readonly automatic: boolean;
  readonly label: string;
  readonly venueTimezone: string;
  readonly scheduledStart: Date | null;
  readonly autoAllowed: boolean;
  readonly destinationName: string | null;
  readonly overlayUrl: string | null;
  readonly pollSeconds: number;
};

/** The broadcast's non-secret fields, while one is held. `cred` never crosses the bridge (A1, A5). */
export type BroadcastInfo = {
  readonly sid: string;
  readonly cause: Cause;
  readonly playbackUrl: string;
  readonly overlayUrl: string | null;
  readonly label: string;
  /** Per transport offered; SRT absent when the server offered none (A18). */
  readonly holdWindowSeconds: Readonly<Partial<Record<Transport, number>>>;
  readonly maxDurationMinutes: number;
  readonly scoreUpdates: ScoreUpdates;
  readonly srtOffered: boolean;
};

/** A refused or failed start, until the next start or the end of the pairing. */
export type Refusal = 'no_destination' | 'no_credit' | 'not_entitled' | 'unknown' | 'start-failed';

/** Why the last broadcast ended without the operator, while back in Paired. */
export type LastEnd =
  | 'stopped-by-organiser'
  | 'stopped-automatically'
  | 'no-signal'
  | 'destination-refused'
  | 'max-duration'
  | 'phone-lost'
  | 'ended-by-seazn'
  | 'hold-window-expired'
  | 'stopped';

/** Why native left a pairing the operator did not end. */
export type UnpairReason = 'code-ended' | 'replaced' | 'taken' | 'permissions';

export type Unpaired = {
  readonly reason: UnpairReason;
  readonly code: string;
  readonly slot: number;
  readonly tokenTag: string;
};
```

import type { SessionState, ShedStep } from '@/domain/session/SessionState';

/** A9: `new` from a scan or Continue, `resume` from the cold-start re-pair only. */
export type Claim = 'new' | 'resume';

/**
 * Everything native needs to pair (amendment, The engine port). `token` is
 * the code's Bearer: a secret, never logged; the bridge protects it on arrival.
 * `language` is the notification's (P3), a two-letter code.

export type PairIntent = {
  readonly kind: 'pair';
  readonly code: string;
  readonly slot: number;

/** Intents, not RPC (AGENTS §2): each returns void, and native ignores one that does not fit. */

  | { readonly kind: 'start' }
  | { readonly kind: 'stop' }
  | { readonly kind: 'unpair' }
  | { readonly kind: 'reset' }
  | { readonly kind: 'setAutomatic'; readonly on: boolean }
  | { readonly kind: 'setLanguage'; readonly language: string }

export type EngineSnapshot = {
  readonly state: SessionState;
  readonly telemetry: Telemetry;
  /** From `pair` until `reset` or Idle; Ended keeps it, so JS can forget the code it names. */
  readonly pairing: PairingInfo | null;
  /** While a broadcast is held. Ended carries none (CD40). */
  readonly broadcast: BroadcastInfo | null;
  readonly ready: Readiness;
  readonly refusal: Refusal | null;
  readonly lastEnd: LastEnd | null;
  /** In Idle after an unpair the operator did not ask for, until the next `pair`. */
  readonly unpaired: Unpaired | null;
  /** A 401 seen while a broadcast is held: "Code ended" follows the broadcast's end. */
  readonly codeEndedPending: boolean;
  readonly camera: CameraState | null;
  readonly reportedAtMs: number;
  readonly survivesBackground: boolean;
};

```ts
import { tokenTag } from '@/domain/credentials/tokenTag';
import type { Readiness } from '@/domain/session/Pairing';
import type { EngineIntent, EngineSnapshot, PairIntent } from '../CaptureEnginePort';
import type { ServerSays } from './serverSays';

/** How a scenario drives an engine: the port's own intents, the server's words, native's readiness. */
export type ScenarioKit = {
  send(intent: EngineIntent): Promise<void>;
  say(words: ServerSays): Promise<void>;
  ready(ready: Partial<Readiness>): Promise<void>;
  snapshot(): EngineSnapshot;
};

export type Scenario = {
  readonly name: string;
  /** Needs the server's words: run on the fake and the JVM host, and on a phone only with Task 34's scripted server. */
  readonly needsServer: boolean;
  run(kit: ScenarioKit): Promise<void>;
};

const pairIntent = (code: string, slot: number, token: string): PairIntent => ({
  kind: 'pair',
  code,
  slot,
  token,
  codeUrl: `https://stg.seazn.club/api/capture/codes/${code}`,
  heartbeatUrl: `https://stg.seazn.club/api/capture/codes/${code}/beat`,
  startUrl: `https://stg.seazn.club/api/capture/codes/${code}/start`,
  language: 'en',
  automatic: true,
  claim: 'new',
  environment: 'staging',
});

/** Two made-up codes: A pairs first, B is another code on another slot. */
export const KIT_CODE_A = pairIntent('kit-a', 1, 'tok-kit-a-0000000000');
export const KIT_CODE_B = pairIntent('kit-b', 2, 'tok-kit-b-0000000000');

const ON_AIR: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set([
  'connecting',
  'publishing',
  'degraded',
  'reconnecting',
]);

const nameOf = (intent: PairIntent) => ({
  code: intent.code,
  slot: intent.slot,
  tokenTag: tokenTag(intent.token),
});

const named = (snapshot: EngineSnapshot) =>
  snapshot.pairing === null
    ? null
    : {
        code: snapshot.pairing.code,
        slot: snapshot.pairing.slot,
        tokenTag: snapshot.pairing.tokenTag,
      };

/** JSON with every object's keys sorted, so the bridge's key order cannot fail a scenario. */
function canonical(value: unknown): string {
  return JSON.stringify(value, (_key, inner: unknown) =>
    inner !== null && typeof inner === 'object' && !Array.isArray(inner)
      ? Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(inner).sort(([a], [b]) => a.localeCompare(b)))
      : inner,
  );
}

/** Throws with what was seen. Names and kinds only: a token is never in a message. */
function same(seen: unknown, wanted: unknown, what: string): void {
  if (canonical(seen) !== canonical(wanted)) {
    throw new Error(`${what}: saw ${canonical(seen)}, wanted ${canonical(wanted)}`);
  }
}

function onAir(kit: ScenarioKit, what: string): void {
  const { kind } = kit.snapshot().state;
  if (!ON_AIR.has(kind)) throw new Error(`${what}: saw ${kind}, wanted a broadcast on air`);
}

const kind = (kit: ScenarioKit) => kit.snapshot().state.kind;

/**
 * The engine contract after the stable code (amendment, The engine port and
 * plan B's core): what JS may rely on from any `CaptureEnginePort`.
 */
export const ENGINE_SCENARIOS: readonly Scenario[] = [
  {
    name: 'pairs from idle, named by code, slot and token tag; a second pair for it changes nothing',
    needsServer: false,
    run: async (kit) => {
      same(kind(kit), 'idle', 'before');
      await kit.send(KIT_CODE_A);
      same(kind(kit), 'paired', 'after pair');
      same(named(kit.snapshot()), nameOf(KIT_CODE_A), 'the name');
      await kit.send(KIT_CODE_A);
      same(kind(kit), 'paired', 'after a second pair');
      same(named(kit.snapshot()), nameOf(KIT_CODE_A), 'the name, kept');
    },
  },
  {
    name: 'pairs another code over a pairing, and holds the new name',
    needsServer: false,
    run: async (kit) => {
      await kit.send(KIT_CODE_A);
      await kit.send(KIT_CODE_B);
      same(kind(kit), 'paired', 'after the second code');
      same(named(kit.snapshot()), nameOf(KIT_CODE_B), 'the new name');
    },
  },
  {
    name: "goes on air from paired on the operator's start; a start from idle does nothing",
    needsServer: false,
    run: async (kit) => {
      await kit.send({ kind: 'start' });
      same(kind(kit), 'idle', 'a start from idle');
      await kit.send(KIT_CODE_A);
      await kit.send({ kind: 'start' });
      onAir(kit, 'after start');
      same(kit.snapshot().broadcast?.cause, 'operator', 'the cause');
    },
  },
  {
    name: "goes on air on the organiser's Go live, with no intent",
    needsServer: true,
    run: async (kit) => {
      await kit.send(KIT_CODE_A);
      await kit.say({ word: 'go-live', cause: 'organiser' });
      onAir(kit, 'after go-live');
      same(kit.snapshot().broadcast?.cause, 'organiser', 'the cause');
    },
  },
  {
    name: 'holds a Go live in armed until the phone is ready, then goes on air',
    needsServer: true,
    run: async (kit) => {
      await kit.send(KIT_CODE_A);
      await kit.ready({ held: false });
      await kit.say({ word: 'go-live', cause: 'automatic' });
      same(
        kit.snapshot().state,
        { kind: 'armed', cause: 'automatic', notReady: 'held' },
        'not held',
      );
      await kit.ready({ held: true });
      onAir(kit, 'once held');
      same(kit.snapshot().broadcast?.cause, 'automatic', 'the cause');
    },
  },
  {
    name: 'stops a broadcast operator-stopped, still naming the pairing; a stop while paired does nothing',
    needsServer: false,
    run: async (kit) => {
      await kit.send(KIT_CODE_A);
      await kit.send({ kind: 'stop' });
      same(kind(kit), 'paired', 'a stop while paired');
      await kit.send({ kind: 'start' });
      await kit.send({ kind: 'stop' });
      const { state } = kit.snapshot();
      same(state.kind === 'ended' ? state.reason : state.kind, 'operator-stopped', 'ended');
      same(named(kit.snapshot()), nameOf(KIT_CODE_A), 'still named');
    },
  },
  {
    name: 'unpairs from paired to idle, naming nothing; an unpair while a broadcast is held does nothing',
    needsServer: false,
    run: async (kit) => {
      await kit.send(KIT_CODE_A);
      await kit.send({ kind: 'start' });
      await kit.send({ kind: 'unpair' });
      onAir(kit, 'an unpair on air');
      await kit.send({ kind: 'stop' });
      await kit.send({ kind: 'reset' });
      await kit.send(KIT_CODE_A);
      await kit.send({ kind: 'unpair' });
      same(kind(kit), 'idle', 'after unpair');
      same(named(kit.snapshot()), null, 'no name');
      same(kit.snapshot().unpaired, null, 'an unpair the operator asked for says no reason');
    },
  },
  {
    name: 'takeover: a replaced answer unpairs to idle, naming the code and the reason',
    needsServer: true,
    run: async (kit) => {
      await kit.send(KIT_CODE_A);
      await kit.say({ word: 'replaced' });
      same(kind(kit), 'idle', 'after replaced');
      same(kit.snapshot().unpaired, { reason: 'replaced', ...nameOf(KIT_CODE_A) }, 'unpaired');
    },
  },
  {
    name: 'rejoin: a live answer while paired goes on air, caused by the rejoin',
    needsServer: true,
    run: async (kit) => {
      await kit.send(KIT_CODE_A);
      await kit.say({ word: 'live' });
      onAir(kit, 'after live');
      same(kit.snapshot().broadcast?.cause, 'rejoin', 'the cause');
    },
  },
  {
    name: "an organiser's stop returns to paired with its last end, and Ended is never shown",
    needsServer: true,
    run: async (kit) => {
      await kit.send(KIT_CODE_A);
      await kit.say({ word: 'go-live', cause: 'organiser' });
      await kit.say({ word: 'over', lastEnd: 'stopped-by-organiser' });
      same(kind(kit), 'paired', 'after over');
      same(kit.snapshot().lastEnd, 'stopped-by-organiser', 'the last end');
      same(kit.snapshot().broadcast, null, 'no broadcast');
    },
  },
  {
    name: 'resets only from ended; a pair in ended is ignored; reset then pair pairs',
    needsServer: false,
    run: async (kit) => {
      await kit.send(KIT_CODE_A);
      await kit.send({ kind: 'reset' });
      same(kind(kit), 'paired', 'a reset while paired');
      await kit.send({ kind: 'start' });
      await kit.send({ kind: 'stop' });
      await kit.send(KIT_CODE_B);
      same(kind(kit), 'ended', 'a pair in ended');
      await kit.send({ kind: 'reset' });
      same([kind(kit), named(kit.snapshot())], ['idle', null], 'after reset');
      await kit.send(KIT_CODE_B);
      same(named(kit.snapshot()), nameOf(KIT_CODE_B), 'paired again');
    },
  },
];

Then the wrapper, `test/engineContract.ts`, replacing today's file whole:

```ts
import { afterEach, beforeEach, describe, it } from 'vitest';
import type { Readiness } from '@/domain/session/Pairing';
import type { CaptureEnginePort } from '@/engine/CaptureEnginePort';
import { ENGINE_SCENARIOS, type ScenarioKit } from '@/engine/contract/engineScenarios';
import type { ServerSays } from '@/engine/contract/serverSays';

/** One engine for one test, the server that answers it, and how to let both go. */
export type EngineUnderTest = {
  readonly engine: CaptureEnginePort;
  say(words: ServerSays): void | Promise<void>;
  ready(ready: Partial<Readiness>): void | Promise<void>;
  dispose(): void | Promise<void>;
};

/**
 * Waits until the engine has reported on what was just sent. The fake reports
 * synchronously, so its default waits for nothing; the bridge waits for the ack (CD8).
 */
export type Settle = () => Promise<void>;
const NOTHING: Settle = () => Promise.resolve();

export function describeEngineContract(
  name: string,
  make: () => EngineUnderTest | Promise<EngineUnderTest>,
  settle: Settle = NOTHING,
): void {
  describe(`the engine contract: ${name}`, () => {
    let subject: EngineUnderTest;
    beforeEach(async () => {
      subject = await make();
    });
    afterEach(() => subject.dispose());
    const kit: ScenarioKit = {
      send: async (intent) => {
        subject.engine.send(intent);
        await settle();
      },
      say: async (words) => {
        await subject.say(words);
        await settle();
      },
      ready: async (ready) => {
        await subject.ready(ready);
        await settle();
      },
      snapshot: () => subject.engine.getSnapshot(),
    };
    for (const scenario of ENGINE_SCENARIOS) it(scenario.name, () => scenario.run(kit));
  });
}
