```ts
    case 'armed-not-ready':
      return {
        state: { kind: 'armed', cause: 'organiser', notReady: 'held' },
        telemetry: ARMED,
        ready: { ...READY, held: false },
      };
    case 'unpaired-replaced':
      return { state: IDLE, telemetry: IDLE_TELEMETRY, ready: NOT_READY };
```

The `stopped` and `fatal` cases keep their `ended(...)` states; `stopped-by-organiser` and the two `armed-*` cases go. Then the engine:

```ts
function telemetryFor(state: SessionState, now: number): Telemetry {
  switch (state.kind) {
    case 'idle':
    case 'pairing':
    case 'ended':
      return IDLE_TELEMETRY;
    case 'paired':
    case 'arming':
    case 'armed':
    case 'connecting':
      return ARMED;
    case 'reconnecting':
      return reconnectingTelemetry(now);
    default:
      return onAir(now);
  }
}

const cameraFor = (state: SessionState): CameraState | null =>
  state.kind === 'idle' || state.kind === 'pairing' || state.kind === 'ended' ? null : 'own';

const sinceOf = (state: SessionState): number | null =>
  'sinceEpochMs' in state ? state.sinceEpochMs : null;

const sameName = (
  pairing: PairingInfo | null,
  name: Pick<PairingInfo, 'code' | 'slot' | 'tokenTag'>,
) =>
  pairing !== null &&
  pairing.code === name.code &&
  pairing.slot === name.slot &&
  pairing.tokenTag === name.tokenTag;

export function createFakeCaptureEngine(now: () => number = Date.now): FakeCaptureEngine {
  let snapshot: EngineSnapshot = {
    ...AT_REST,
    state: IDLE,
    telemetry: IDLE_TELEMETRY,
    ready: NOT_READY,
    camera: null,
    reportedAtMs: now(),
    survivesBackground: false,
  };
  const primary: Transport = 'srt';
  let permissions: PermissionAnswer = 'grant';
  let waiting: Partial<PairingInfo> = {};
  const intentKinds: EngineIntent['kind'][] = [];
  const listeners = new Set<() => void>();
  let pending: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null = null;
  let report: ReturnType<typeof setInterval> | null = null;

  const publish = (next: Partial<EngineSnapshot>): void => {
    snapshot = { ...snapshot, ...next, reportedAtMs: now() };
    for (const listener of listeners) listener();
  };
  const show = (state: SessionState, extra: Partial<EngineSnapshot> = {}): void =>
    publish({ state, telemetry: telemetryFor(state, now()), camera: cameraFor(state), ...extra });
  const cancelPending = (): void => {
    if (pending !== null) clearTimeout(pending);
    pending = null;
  };
  const later = (afterMs: number, next: () => SessionState): void => {
    pending = setTimeout(() => {
      pending = null;
      show(next());
    }, afterMs);
  };
  const atRest = (extra: Partial<EngineSnapshot> = {}): void => {
    cancelPending();
    show(IDLE, { ...AT_REST, ready: NOT_READY, ...extra });
  };

  const paired = (pairing: PairingInfo): void =>
    show({ kind: 'paired' }, { ...AT_REST, pairing, ready: READY });

  const unpaired = (reason: UnpairReason): void => {
    const pairing = snapshot.pairing;
    if (pairing === null) return;
    const { code, slot, tokenTag: tag } = pairing;
    atRest({ unpaired: { reason, code, slot, tokenTag: tag } });
  };

  const pair = (intent: PairIntent): void => {
    const { kind } = snapshot.state;
    if (BROADCAST.has(kind) || kind === 'ended') return;
    const name = { code: intent.code, slot: intent.slot, tokenTag: tokenTag(intent.token) };
    if ((kind === 'pairing' || kind === 'paired') && sameName(snapshot.pairing, name)) return;
    const pairing: PairingInfo = {
      ...FAKE_PAIRING,
      ...waiting,
      ...name,
      automatic: intent.automatic,
    };
    if (permissions === 'refuse') return atRest({ unpaired: { reason: 'permissions', ...name } });
    if (permissions === 'hold')
      return show({ kind: 'pairing' }, { ...AT_REST, pairing, ready: NOT_READY });
    paired(pairing);
  };

  const connect = (broadcast: BroadcastInfo): void => {
    show({ kind: 'connecting', transport: primary }, { broadcast, refusal: null, lastEnd: null });
    later(CONNECT_MS, () => publishing(primary, now()));
  };

  /** A start, remote or held: Armed waits for readiness, as native's gate does (A11). */
  const goLive = (cause: Cause): void => {
    const broadcast = snapshot.broadcast ?? broadcastFor(snapshot.pairing ?? FAKE_PAIRING, cause);
    const notReady = firstNotReady(snapshot.ready);
    if (notReady !== null) {
      return show({ kind: 'armed', cause, notReady }, { broadcast, refusal: null, lastEnd: null });
    }
    connect(broadcast);
  };

  const start = (): void => {
    if (snapshot.state.kind !== 'paired' || firstNotReady(snapshot.ready) !== null) return;
    goLive('operator');
  };

  const stop = (): void => {
    if (!BROADCAST.has(snapshot.state.kind)) return;
    cancelPending();
    const since = sinceOf(snapshot.state);
    show(ended('operator-stopped', since === null ? null : now() - since), { broadcast: null });
  };

  const unpair = (): void => {
    const { kind } = snapshot.state;
    if (kind === 'pairing' || kind === 'paired') atRest();
  };

  const reset = (): void => {
    if (snapshot.state.kind === 'ended') atRest();
  };

  /** The broadcast ends without the operator: back to Paired with why, or out on a pending 401. */
  const over = (lastEnd: LastEnd): void => {
    if (!BROADCAST.has(snapshot.state.kind)) return;
    cancelPending();
    if (snapshot.codeEndedPending) return unpaired('code-ended');
    show({ kind: 'paired' }, { broadcast: null, lastEnd });
  };

  const hear = (says: ServerSays): void => {
    const { kind } = snapshot.state;
    const isPaired = kind === 'paired';
    switch (says.word) {
      case 'go-live':
        return isPaired ? goLive(says.cause) : undefined;
      case 'live':
        return isPaired ? goLive('rejoin') : undefined;
      case 'over':
        return over(says.lastEnd);
      case 'refused':
        return isPaired ? publish({ refusal: says.refusal }) : undefined;
      case 'replaced':
        return unpaired('replaced');
      case 'taken':
        return isPaired || kind === 'pairing' ? unpaired('taken') : undefined;
      case 'code-ended':
        return BROADCAST.has(kind) ? publish({ codeEndedPending: true }) : unpaired('code-ended');
    }
  };

  const setReady = (change: Partial<Readiness>): void => {
    const ready = { ...snapshot.ready, ...change };
    const { state } = snapshot;
    if (state.kind !== 'armed') return publish({ ready });
    const notReady = firstNotReady(ready);
    publish({ ready, state: { ...state, notReady } });
    if (notReady === null && snapshot.broadcast !== null) connect(snapshot.broadcast);
  };

  const setPermissions = (answer: PermissionAnswer): void => {
    permissions = answer;
    if (snapshot.state.kind !== 'pairing' || snapshot.pairing === null || answer === 'hold') return;
    if (answer === 'grant') return paired(snapshot.pairing);
    unpaired('permissions');
  };

  const automatic = (on: boolean): void => {
    const { pairing, state } = snapshot;
    if (pairing !== null && state.kind !== 'ended')
      publish({ pairing: { ...pairing, automatic: on } });
  };

  const play = (scene: Scene): void => {
    cancelPending();
    const held = snapshot.pairing ?? { ...FAKE_PAIRING, ...waiting };
    const resting = scene.state.kind === 'idle';
    publish({
      ...AT_REST,
      state: scene.state,
      telemetry: scene.telemetry,
      camera: scene.camera ?? cameraFor(scene.state),
      ready: scene.ready ?? READY,
      pairing: resting ? null : held,
      broadcast: BROADCAST.has(scene.state.kind)
        ? (snapshot.broadcast ?? broadcastFor(held, 'operator'))
        : null,
      unpaired: resting
        ? { reason: 'replaced', code: held.code, slot: held.slot, tokenTag: held.tokenTag }
        : null,
      ...scene.extra,
    });
    const { then } = scene;
    if (then !== undefined) later(then.afterMs, () => then.state);
  };

  const send = (intent: EngineIntent): void => {
    intentKinds.push(intent.kind);
    if (intentKinds.length > INTENT_LOG_CAP) intentKinds.shift();
    switch (intent.kind) {
      case 'pair':
        return pair(intent);
      case 'start':
        return start();
      case 'stop':
        return stop();
      case 'unpair':
        return unpair();
      case 'reset':
        return reset();
      case 'setAutomatic':
        return automatic(intent.on);
      case 'setLanguage':
      case 'switchCamera':
        return;
    }
  };

  const stopReporting = (): void => {
    if (report !== null) clearInterval(report);
    report = null;
  };
  report = setInterval(() => publish({}), REPORT_MS);

  return {
    send,
    subscribe: (onChange) => {
      listeners.add(onChange);
      return () => listeners.delete(onChange);
    },
    getSnapshot: () => snapshot,
    intentKinds,
    scene: (name) => play(sceneOf(name, now())),
    forceState: (state) => {
      cancelPending();
      show(state);
    },
    hear,
    setReady,
    setPermissions,
    setPairing: (change) => {
      waiting = { ...waiting, ...change };
      if (snapshot.pairing !== null) publish({ pairing: { ...snapshot.pairing, ...change } });
    },
    patch: (telemetry) => publish({ telemetry: { ...snapshot.telemetry, ...telemetry } }),
    setCamera: (camera) => publish({ camera }),
    suspend: () => {
      cancelPending();
      stopReporting();
    },
    dispose: () => {
      cancelPending();
      stopReporting();
    },
  };
}
```

`createFakeCaptureEngine` is over the 25-line guide, as the old one was: it is the fake's state table, written as one closure so the timers and listeners have one owner (AGENTS §12's exemption for transition tables). `FakeCaptureEngine.test.ts`: delete the `arm`-path tests and the `setDescriptor`/`setSlot`/`setTokenTag` tests; keep the scene, report-timer, `suspend`, `dispose` and intent-log tests, with the renamed scenes; add one test per new rule the kit does not reach: a second `pair` for the held code keeps its `refusal` (pair, `hear({ word: 'refused', refusal: 'no_credit' })`, pair again: `refusal` is still `no_credit`); `start` with `sound: false` stays paired; `setPermissions('hold')` keeps Pairing and `'grant'` then pairs; `'refuse'` is Idle with `unpaired.reason` `permissions`; `code-ended` while live sets `codeEndedPending` and the following `over` unpairs with `code-ended`; `setAutomatic(false)` echoes in `pairing.automatic`; every scene in `FAKE_SCENES` plays without throwing and `unpaired-replaced` names the held code.

  2. `recognise.ts`: `recogniseStream` keys on `code`, not `sid`, and parses with `parseStreamCode`:

```ts
/**
 * capture-qr v2 after the stable code (A1): `{v:2, code, slot, tok, exp?}`. A
 * higher version that still names a code asks for an update. A pre-amendment
 * v2, with a sid and credentials but no code, is not a code this app reads.
 */
function recogniseStream(raw: string, text: string, now: Date): Recognition {
  const data = parseJson(text);
  if (!isRecord(data) || !isNonEmptyString(data.code)) return FOREIGN;
  if (isInteger(data.v) && data.v > 2) return { outcome: 'newerVersion', mode: 'stream' };
  const parsed = parseStreamCode(data);
  if (!parsed.ok) return FOREIGN;
  const { expiresAt } = parsed.value;
  if (expiresAt !== null && expiresAt.getTime() <= now.getTime()) {
    return { outcome: 'expired', mode: 'stream', at: expiresAt };
  }
  return { outcome: 'code', code: { mode: 'stream', raw, ...parsed.value } };
}
```

```ts
import {
  parseWaitingFields,
  waitingToWire,
  type WaitingFields,
} from '@/domain/credentials/waitingFields';
import { httpsHost, isRecord } from '@/domain/credentials/wire';
import type { Mode, ModeCode } from '@/domain/mode/Mode';

/**
 * What a stream code keeps beside the QR (amendment §3): the waiting fields
 * and the three URLs (`codeUrl` here, the beat and start URLs in `waiting`),
 * so a cold start can re-pair with no fetch. Never `cred`. `tapToPair` marks
 * a code whose pairing failed permanently: only Continue re-pairs it (Task 24).
 */
export type SavedStream = {
  readonly waiting: WaitingFields;
  readonly codeUrl: string;
  readonly tapToPair: boolean;
};

export type SavedCode = {
  readonly mode: Mode;
  /** The QR whole. A stream code's holds `tok`: never log it. */
  readonly raw: string;
  /** Stream codes only: shown on the Continue card and the stream screen. */
  readonly slot: number | null;
  readonly savedAt: Date;
  /** The QR's `exp`, or null when it has none (A1) and for other modes. */
  readonly expiresAt: Date | null;
  /** Stream codes only, and required for them: a stream record without one is dropped. */
  readonly stream: SavedStream | null;
};

const VERSION = 3;

export function savedCodeFrom(code: ModeCode, now: Date, stream: SavedStream | null): SavedCode {
  const isStream = code.mode === 'stream';
  return {
    mode: code.mode,
    raw: code.raw,
    slot: isStream ? code.slot : null,
    savedAt: now,
    expiresAt: isStream ? code.expiresAt : null,
    stream: isStream ? stream : null,
  };
}

export function venueZone(code: SavedCode): string | null {
  return code.stream?.waiting.venueTimezone || null;
}
```

`encodeSavedCode` writes `v: 3` and `stream: code.stream === null ? null : { waiting: waitingToWire(code.stream.waiting), codeUrl: code.stream.codeUrl, tapToPair: code.stream.tapToPair }` in place of `descriptor`. `decodeSavedCode` checks `data.v !== VERSION` (so a v2 record, which held credentials, is dropped: S0 decision 12's clean slate, as D28 did for v1), and replaces `decodeDescriptor` with:

```ts
/** `false` is present but unreadable, which drops the whole record. */
function decodeStream(value: unknown): SavedStream | null | false {
  if (value === null || value === undefined) return null;
  if (
    !isRecord(value) ||
    typeof value.codeUrl !== 'string' ||
    typeof value.tapToPair !== 'boolean'
  ) {
    return false;
  }
  // The code's URL was built from the build's origin at the scan, so its host is the one to trust.
  const waiting = parseWaitingFields(value.waiting, httpsHost(value.codeUrl) ?? '');
  return waiting === null ? false : { waiting, codeUrl: value.codeUrl, tapToPair: value.tapToPair };
}
```

```ts
import { parseStreamCodeText } from '@/domain/credentials/streamCode';
import { tokenTag } from '@/domain/credentials/tokenTag';
import type { SavedCode } from '@/domain/mode/savedCode';

/**
 * What names a stream code (amendment, Identity rules in JS): its code, its
 * camera position (`slot`, C7) and its issue (`tokenTag`, N2, never the
 * token). Null where it is not known: no pairing, or a code the phone cannot read.
 */
export type CodeName = {
  readonly code: string | null;
  readonly slot: number | null;
  readonly tokenTag: string | null;
};

export const NO_NAME: CodeName = { code: null, slot: null, tokenTag: null };

/** The same code: all three named on both sides and equal. A null never matches. */
export function sameCode(held: CodeName, code: CodeName): boolean {
  return (
    held.code !== null &&
    held.code === code.code &&
    held.slot !== null &&
    held.slot === code.slot &&
    held.tokenTag !== null &&
    held.tokenTag === code.tokenTag
  );
}

/** A saved code's name, read from its QR. The token goes no further than this call. */
export function savedCodeName(saved: SavedCode): CodeName {
  const code = parseStreamCodeText(saved.raw);
  if (!code.ok) return NO_NAME;
  return { code: code.value.code, slot: code.value.slot, tokenTag: tokenTag(code.value.token) };
}
```

```ts
import { sameCode, type CodeName } from '@/domain/mode/codeName';
import type { EngineStatus } from '@/domain/mode/reopen';

/** What a scan or Continue does with the engine it finds (amendment, Identity rules in JS). */
export type ScanStep = 'adopt' | 'pair' | 'resetThenPair' | 'none';

/**
 * - the same code while paired: adopt, no intent;
 * - another code or slot while paired, or an idle engine: `pair` (native unpairs first);
 * - an ended engine: `reset` then `pair`, since native ignores a `pair` in Ended and
 *   applies intents in order;
 * - a held broadcast: nothing (cannot happen: Home is hidden, AGENTS §6).
 */
export function scanStep(input: {
  engine: EngineStatus;
  held: CodeName;
  code: CodeName;
}): ScanStep {
  switch (input.engine) {
    case 'live':
      return 'none';
    case 'stopped':
    case 'failed':
      return 'resetThenPair';
    case 'paired':
      return sameCode(input.held, input.code) ? 'adopt' : 'pair';
    case 'idle':
      return 'pair';
  }
}
```

```ts
import { useEffect, useMemo } from 'react';
import { parseStreamCodeText } from '@/domain/credentials/streamCode';
import { usePorts } from '@/hooks/usePorts';
import { useSavedStream } from '@/hooks/useSavedStream';

/**
 * CD6 as the amendment rewrites it: the code's token is in hand from the scan
 * to the unpair, not only while the viewfinder shows. The scan protects it at
 * once (useCodeCheck); this keeps it protected while the code is saved, and
 * releases it when the code is forgotten (Task 10's N7).
 */
export function useProtectCode(): void {
  const { logger } = usePorts();
  const saved = useSavedStream();
  const token = useMemo(() => {
    const code = saved === null ? null : parseStreamCodeText(saved.raw);
    return code?.ok ? code.value.token : null;
  }, [saved]);
  useEffect(() => {
    if (token === null) return undefined;
    logger.protect({ secrets: [token], streamIds: [] });
    return () => logger.release();
  }, [token, logger]);
}
```

```ts
import { useCallback } from 'react';
import { parseStreamCodeText } from '@/domain/credentials/streamCode';
import { savedCodeName } from '@/domain/mode/codeName';
import { scanStep } from '@/domain/mode/identity';
import type { SavedCode } from '@/domain/mode/savedCode';
import type { Environment } from '@/domain/session/Pairing';
import type { Claim, PairIntent } from '@/engine/CaptureEnginePort';
import { selectEngineStatus, selectHeldName } from '@/hooks/engineSelectors';
import { useLanguage } from '@/hooks/useLanguage';
import { usePorts } from '@/hooks/usePorts';

type PairFacts = {
  readonly language: string;
  readonly automatic: boolean;
  readonly environment: Environment;
  readonly claim: Claim;
};

/** The pair intent for a saved stream code, or null when the code cannot be used. */
export function pairIntentFor(saved: SavedCode, facts: PairFacts): PairIntent | null {
  const code = parseStreamCodeText(saved.raw);
  if (!code.ok || saved.stream === null) return null;
  const { codeUrl, waiting } = saved.stream;
  return {
    kind: 'pair',
    code: code.value.code,
    slot: code.value.slot,
    token: code.value.token,
    codeUrl,
    heartbeatUrl: waiting.heartbeatUrl,
    startUrl: waiting.startUrl,
    ...facts,
  };
}

/**
 * Pairs the engine with a saved code, by the identity rules (scanStep). Every
 * `pair` is the operator's (a scan or Continue, claim `new`) or the cold-start
 * re-pair (`resume`, Task 24); nothing else calls this.
 */
export function usePairing(): (saved: SavedCode, claim: Claim) => void {
  const { engine, logger, streamSettings, environment } = usePorts();
  const { lang } = useLanguage();
  return useCallback(
    (saved: SavedCode, claim: Claim) => {
      const facts = {
        language: lang,
        automatic: streamSettings.getSnapshot().automatic,
        environment,
        claim,
      };
      const intent = pairIntentFor(saved, facts);
      if (intent === null) return logger.warn('stream.unusable-code');
      const snapshot = engine.getSnapshot();
      const held = selectHeldName(snapshot);
      const step = scanStep({
        engine: selectEngineStatus(snapshot),
        held,
        code: savedCodeName(saved),
      });
      logger.info('intent.pair', { action: step, mode: claim, slot: intent.slot });
      if (step === 'adopt' || step === 'none') return;
      if (step === 'resetThenPair') engine.send({ kind: 'reset' });
      engine.send(intent);
    },
    [engine, logger, streamSettings, environment, lang],
  );
}
```

```ts
function useOpenCode(setStatusKey: SetStatusKey, saveFailed: SaveFailed): OpenCode {
  const { modeStore, clock, navigation } = usePorts();
  const pair = usePairing();
  return useCallback(
    async (code: ModeCode, stream: SavedStream | null) => {
      if (!isReady(modeStore)) return;
      const saved = savedCodeFrom(code, clock(), stream);
      try {
        await modeStore.open(saved);
      } catch {
        return saveFailed('open');
      }
      setStatusKey(null);
      if (code.mode !== 'stream') return;
      // Amendment §2's outcome table: saved, then /stream, then pair.
      navigation.go('stream');
      pair(saved, 'new');
    },
    [modeStore, clock, navigation, pair, setStatusKey, saveFailed],
  );
}
```

```ts
export function selectOnAirPhase(snapshot: EngineSnapshot): OnAirPhase {
  switch (snapshot.state.kind) {
    case 'idle':
    case 'pairing':
    case 'ended':
      return 'idle';
    case 'paired':
      return 'ready';
    case 'arming':
    case 'armed':
    case 'connecting':
    case 'publishing':
      return 'live';
    case 'degraded':
    case 'reconnecting':
      return 'trouble';
  }
}

export function selectEngineStatus(snapshot: EngineSnapshot): EngineStatus {
  const { state } = snapshot;
  switch (state.kind) {
    case 'idle':
      return 'idle';
    case 'pairing':
    case 'paired':
      return 'paired';
    case 'ended':
      return state.reason === 'operator-stopped' ? 'stopped' : 'failed';
    default:
      return 'live';
  }
}

/** The camera is open while paired (CD37), so the lock holds from Paired on, as it did from Armed. */
export function selectHoldsOrientation(snapshot: EngineSnapshot): boolean {
  const status = selectEngineStatus(snapshot);
  return status === 'paired' || status === 'live';
}

export const selectOverlayUrl = (snapshot: EngineSnapshot) =>
  snapshot.broadcast?.overlayUrl ?? snapshot.pairing?.overlayUrl ?? null;
export const selectPlaybackUrl = (snapshot: EngineSnapshot) =>
  snapshot.broadcast?.playbackUrl ?? null;
export const selectScoreUpdates = (snapshot: EngineSnapshot) =>
  snapshot.broadcast?.scoreUpdates ?? null;
/** Pairing's label is empty until the claim is answered: read as none. */
export const selectLabel = (snapshot: EngineSnapshot) =>
  snapshot.broadcast?.label || snapshot.pairing?.label || null;
export const selectVenueZone = (snapshot: EngineSnapshot) =>
  snapshot.pairing?.venueTimezone || null;
export const selectHasPairing = (snapshot: EngineSnapshot) => snapshot.pairing !== null;
export const selectHeldCode = (snapshot: EngineSnapshot) => snapshot.pairing?.code ?? null;
export const selectHeldSlot = (snapshot: EngineSnapshot) => snapshot.pairing?.slot ?? null;
export const selectHeldTokenTag = (snapshot: EngineSnapshot) => snapshot.pairing?.tokenTag ?? null;

/** For one-off reads (usePairing), never for useEngineSelector: a new object each call. */
export function selectHeldName(snapshot: EngineSnapshot): CodeName {
  const { pairing } = snapshot;
  return pairing === null
    ? NO_NAME
    : { code: pairing.code, slot: pairing.slot, tokenTag: pairing.tokenTag };
}
```

**The four questions.** (1) A second call: a second scan before the first settles is `scanFlight`'s, unchanged; a second `pair` for the same code is adopted in JS and ignored in native (kit scenario 1); Continue on a paired code adopts. (2) An empty input: a QR with no `exp`; a saved record of v2, or with no `stream` part (dropped); a code whose `raw` no longer parses (`pairIntentFor` null, a record line); no network at the scan (Task 22's port). (3) After an interruption: an Ended engine meets a new scan with `reset` then `pair`, in order; a process death is Task 24's. (4) Another mode, orientation or language: a scoring code saves `stream: null` and never pairs; the pair intent carries the current language; the orientation lock now holds from Paired.

```bash
feat(stream): switch to the paired engine; Home pairs, a visit never does

The port carries pair/start/stop/unpair/reset/setAutomatic/setLanguage
and a snapshot of pairing, broadcast and readiness; cred never reaches
JS (A1, A5). StreamSession, the descriptor and its parsers leave JS. The
saved code is v3: the QR, the waiting fields and the three URLs. The fake
gains the paired phase and scripted server words; the kit gains pair,
start, takeover, rejoin and unpair, as data the device probe can run.
Tests of the arm-on-visit, replace and warming-deadline paths are
deleted with the paths; the batch report lists them by file.
```

**The rules, each with its source.**

| Rule                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | Source                                             |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| The re-pair runs once, at cold start, when JS finds the engine Idle, with claim `resume`, only if the active mode is `stream`, a stream code is saved and unexpired, it is not `tapToPair`, and the snapshot's `unpaired` does not name it.                                                                                                   | Process death and reopen                           |
| A foreground never re-pairs: closing the permission dialog reads as one.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | Process death and reopen, _Why only at cold start_ |
| A visit never pairs: reaching `/stream` by a reopen, a route rule or Back sends no intent.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | Process death and reopen                           |
| A held broadcast reopens into `/stream`; so does a paired engine with its code saved. An Idle engine reopens into `/stream` only when the re-pair was sent; any other Idle engine with a saved code goes Home, to the Continue card. A permanent failure (`failed`) with its code kept reopens into `/stream`, to the Ended screen it was on. | `reopenTarget`                                     |
| A paired engine with no saved code is an orphan, unpaired on the way Home. A held broadcast is never an orphan. An Ended engine whose code is gone or expired is cleared.                                                                                                                                                                     | `orphanedSession`, extended                        |
| JS forgets the saved code when the snapshot's `unpaired` names it, or when the snapshot is Ended `operator-stopped` naming it. It compares identities, not two snapshots.                                                                                                                                                                     | The engine port                                    |
| JS marks the saved code `tapToPair` when the snapshot is Ended `fatal-error` naming it, and clears the mark once the snapshot is Paired naming it.                                                                                                                                                                                            | `tapToPair`                                        |
| While the engine holds a broadcast, the app shows `/stream`, whatever screen it was on: a rule on every state change, not only at launch.                                                                                                                                                                                                     | The route follows a broadcast                      |
| Forget sends `unpair`, and forgets the code once the snapshot is Idle; if a broadcast became held instead, it keeps the code. Bounded at 5 s.                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Identity rules in JS, CD26                         |
| A second scan while a `pair` is in flight wins: native applies the intents in order.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | Identity rules in JS                               |

```ts
/**
 * Where the app lands on launch and on every return to the foreground. The
 * engine wins while its process lives (amendment, Process death and reopen):
 * a held broadcast always reopens into /stream, and a paired engine does
 * while its code is saved. An Idle engine reopens into /stream only when the
 * cold-start re-pair was sent (`resumed`); any other Idle engine with a saved
 * code goes Home, to the Continue card. A permanent failure keeps its code and
 * its Ended screen ("Your code is kept").
 */
export function reopenTarget(input: {
  engine: EngineStatus;
  saved: SavedState;
  now: Date;
  resumed: boolean;
}): ReopenTarget {
  const { engine, saved, now } = input;
  const code = saved.codes.stream;
  if (engine === 'live') return { go: 'stream' };
  if (engine === 'paired') return { go: code === undefined ? 'home' : 'stream' };
  if (input.resumed) return { go: 'stream' };
  if (saved.active !== 'stream' || code === undefined) return { go: 'home' };
  if (code.expiresAt !== null && isExpired(code, now)) {
    return {
      go: 'home',
      notice: { mode: 'stream', expiredAt: code.expiresAt, venueTz: venueZone(code) },
    };
  }
  return { go: engine === 'failed' ? 'stream' : 'home' };
}

/**
 * An orphan is cleared on the way Home (I1, N4, extended by the amendment): a
 * paired engine with no saved code is unpaired, and an Ended engine whose code
 * is gone or expired is reset. A held broadcast is never an orphan: the route
 * rule shows it, and only the operator's Stop ends it.
 */
export function orphanedSession(input: {
  engine: EngineStatus;
  saved: SavedState;
  now: Date;
}): boolean {
  const { engine, saved, now } = input;
  const code = saved.codes.stream;
  if (engine === 'paired') return code === undefined;
  if (engine !== 'stopped' && engine !== 'failed') return false;
  return code === undefined || isExpired(code, now);
}

/** The cold-start re-pair's four conditions, on an Idle engine (amendment, Process death and reopen). */
export function resumesAtColdStart(input: {
  engine: EngineStatus;
  unpaired: CodeName | null;
  saved: SavedState;
  now: Date;
}): boolean {
  const code = input.saved.codes.stream;
  if (input.engine !== 'idle' || input.saved.active !== 'stream' || code === undefined)
    return false;
  if (isExpired(code, input.now) || code.stream === null || code.stream.tapToPair) return false;
  return input.unpaired === null || !sameCode(input.unpaired, savedCodeName(code));
}

/**
 * JS forgets the saved code when native says its pairing ended (amendment, The
 * engine port): `unpaired` names it, or Ended `operator-stopped` does. Identity,
 * not a comparison of two snapshots, so it is idempotent.
 */
export function forgetsSaved(input: {
  saved: CodeName;
  unpaired: CodeName | null;
  stopped: CodeName | null;
}): boolean {
  const names = (other: CodeName | null) => other !== null && sameCode(other, input.saved);
  return names(input.unpaired) || names(input.stopped);
}

export type TapMark = 'mark' | 'clear' | null;

/**
 * `tapToPair` (amendment): set when the snapshot shows Ended `fatal-error` for
 * the saved code, so the cold-start re-pair skips it and only Continue re-pairs
 * it; cleared once the snapshot shows that code Paired.
 */
export function tapToPairMark(input: {
  saved: CodeName;
  marked: boolean;
  failed: CodeName | null;
  paired: CodeName | null;
}): TapMark {
  if (!input.marked && input.failed !== null && sameCode(input.failed, input.saved)) return 'mark';
  if (input.marked && input.paired !== null && sameCode(input.paired, input.saved)) return 'clear';
  return null;
}
```

```ts
import { useCallback, useEffect, useRef } from 'react';
import type { EngineStatus } from '@/domain/mode/reopen';
import type { CaptureEnginePort } from '@/engine/CaptureEnginePort';
import { selectEngineStatus } from '@/hooks/engineSelectors';
import { usePorts } from '@/hooks/usePorts';
import type { Logger } from '@/services/logger';

/** CD26: an unpair native never answers is given up, so the engine is never locked for good. */
export const UNPAIR_GIVE_UP_MS = 5_000;

export type UnpairCause = 'forget' | 'orphan' | 'otherMode';
/** `held`: a remote Go live raced the unpair; native ignored it, and the broadcast stands. */
export type UnpairOutcome = 'idle' | 'held' | 'gave-up';
type Done = (outcome: UnpairOutcome) => void;

const underWay = new WeakMap<CaptureEnginePort, () => void>();

/**
 * Moves the engine to Idle without touching a broadcast: `unpair` while paired,
 * `reset` once Ended, one intent per snapshot (intents, not RPC). One clearing
 * per engine at a time; a second call while one is under way is dropped.
 */
export function useUnpair(): (cause: UnpairCause, done?: Done) => void {
  const { engine, logger } = usePorts();
  const mine = useRef<(() => void) | null>(null);
  useEffect(() => () => mine.current?.(), []);
  return useCallback(
    (cause: UnpairCause, done?: Done) => {
      if (underWay.has(engine)) return;
      const finished = () => {
        underWay.delete(engine);
        mine.current = null;
      };
      const end = clear({ engine, logger }, cause, (outcome) => {
        finished();
        done?.(outcome);
      });
      if (end === null) return;
      underWay.set(engine, end);
      mine.current = end;
    },
    [engine, logger],
  );
}

function clearStep(status: EngineStatus): 'unpair' | 'reset' | UnpairOutcome {
  if (status === 'paired') return 'unpair';
  if (status === 'stopped' || status === 'failed') return 'reset';
  return status === 'live' ? 'held' : 'idle';
}

function clear(
  { engine, logger }: { engine: CaptureEnginePort; logger: Logger },
  cause: UnpairCause,
  onDone: Done,
): (() => void) | null {
  let acted: EngineStatus | null = null;
  let ended = false;
  let unsubscribe: () => void = () => undefined;
  const end = (outcome: UnpairOutcome) => {
    if (ended) return;
    ended = true;
    clearTimeout(timer);
    unsubscribe();
    onDone(outcome);
  };
  // Created before the first step: `end` may run inside it (P9).
  const timer = setTimeout(() => {
    logger.warn('unpair.gave-up', { action: cause });
    end('gave-up');
  }, UNPAIR_GIVE_UP_MS);
  const step = () => {
    const status = selectEngineStatus(engine.getSnapshot());
    if (status === acted) return;
    acted = status;
    const next = clearStep(status);
    if (next !== 'unpair' && next !== 'reset') return end(next);
    logger.info(`intent.${next}`, { action: cause });
    engine.send({ kind: next });
  };
  unsubscribe = engine.subscribe(step);
  step();
  return ended ? null : () => end('gave-up');
}
```

The unmount cleanup (`mine.current?.()`) ends the clearing as `gave-up` without a record line, as today's ends it silently. `useReopenGate` and `useHome` import `useUnpair` in place of `useDisarm`.

```ts
/**
 * Forget (amendment, Identity rules in JS): unpair, and forget the code once
 * the engine is Idle. If a remote Go live raced the tap, the broadcast stands,
 * the code is kept, and the route rule shows /stream. A give-up forgets: the
 * operator asked, and an engine still paired is then an orphan, unpaired at the
 * next settle.
 */
function useForget(setStatusKey: SetStatusKey, saveFailed: SaveFailed): () => void {
  const { modeStore } = usePorts();
  const unpair = useUnpair();
  return useCallback(() => {
    unpair('forget', (outcome) => {
      if (outcome === 'held') return;
      void modeStore.forget('stream').then(
        () => setStatusKey(null),
        () => saveFailed('forget'),
      );
    });
  }, [modeStore, setStatusKey, saveFailed, unpair]);
}
```

```ts
import { useEffect, useRef } from 'react';
import { NO_NAME, savedCodeName, type CodeName } from '@/domain/mode/codeName';
import { forgetsSaved, tapToPairMark } from '@/domain/mode/reopen';
import type { SavedCode } from '@/domain/mode/savedCode';
import type { EngineSnapshot } from '@/engine/CaptureEnginePort';
import { selectEngineStatus, selectHeldName } from '@/hooks/engineSelectors';
import { usePorts } from '@/hooks/usePorts';

const nameIf = (on: boolean, snapshot: EngineSnapshot): CodeName | null =>
  on ? selectHeldName(snapshot) : null;

/** The snapshot's facts the saved-code rules read. */
function factsOf(snapshot: EngineSnapshot) {
  const { state, unpaired } = snapshot;
  return {
    unpaired:
      unpaired === null
        ? null
        : { code: unpaired.code, slot: unpaired.slot, tokenTag: unpaired.tokenTag },
    stopped: nameIf(state.kind === 'ended' && state.reason === 'operator-stopped', snapshot),
    failed: nameIf(state.kind === 'ended' && state.reason === 'fatal-error', snapshot),
    paired: nameIf(state.kind === 'paired', snapshot),
  };
}

/**
 * Applies native's word to what JS keeps, on every snapshot (amendment, The
 * engine port and Process death and reopen): forget the code an unasked unpair
 * or the operator's Stop names; mark or clear `tapToPair`; and show /stream
 * while a broadcast is held, from wherever the app is. Each write is made once
 * per saved code (`acted`), so 1 Hz snapshots never queue a write each.
 */
export function useEngineFollow(): void {
  const { engine, modeStore, navigation, logger } = usePorts();
  const acted = useRef<{ code: SavedCode; did: string } | null>(null);
  useEffect(() => {
    const once = (code: SavedCode, did: string, write: () => Promise<void>) => {
      if (acted.current?.code === code && acted.current.did === did) return;
      acted.current = { code, did };
      write().catch(() => logger.warn('store.write-refused', { action: did }));
    };
    const follow = () => {
      const snapshot = engine.getSnapshot();
      if (selectEngineStatus(snapshot) === 'live' && navigation.current() === 'home')
        navigation.go('stream');
      const store = modeStore.getSnapshot();
      const code = store.status === 'ready' ? store.saved.codes.stream : undefined;
      if (code === undefined || code.stream === null) return;
      const facts = factsOf(snapshot);
      const name = savedCodeName(code);
      if (name === NO_NAME) return;
      if (forgetsSaved({ saved: name, ...facts })) {
        // An unpair the operator did not ask for goes Home, to its panel (Task 29); their Stop stays on Ended.
        const home = facts.unpaired !== null;
        return once(code, 'forget', () =>
          modeStore.forget('stream').then(() => (home ? navigation.go('home') : undefined)),
        );
      }
      const mark = tapToPairMark({ saved: name, marked: code.stream.tapToPair, ...facts });
      if (mark !== null) once(code, mark, () => modeStore.markTapToPair(mark === 'mark'));
    };
    const offEngine = engine.subscribe(follow);
    const offStore = modeStore.subscribe(follow);
    follow();
    return () => {
      offEngine();
      offStore();
    };
  }, [engine, modeStore, navigation, logger]);
}
```

`navigation.current() === 'home'` is the route rule's whole test: the stream route and its two sub-routes are already `/stream` (M22), and a repeated `go` is free (`devicePorts.ts`). The amendment's "the claim answered `replaced`: Home, the code forgotten, the panel" is the `home` branch: the forget is the write, and the move follows it, once. - [ ] **Step 7: The cold-start re-pair.** In `useReopenGate.ts`, `useSettle` returns `(coldStart: boolean) => void`; the first decision calls `settle(true)` and every foreground `settle(false)`:

```ts
function useSettle(): (coldStart: boolean) => void {
  const { modeStore, engine, navigation, clock, logger } = usePorts();
  const unpair = useUnpair();
  const pair = usePairing();
  return useCallback(
    (coldStart: boolean) => {
      const current = modeStore.getSnapshot();
      if (current.status !== 'ready') return;
      const snapshot = engine.getSnapshot();
      const facts = { engine: selectEngineStatus(snapshot), saved: current.saved };
      const now = clock();
      const stream = current.saved.codes.stream;
      const unpaired = snapshot.unpaired === null ? null : selectUnpairedName(snapshot);
      // Ruling 3 and R2, for a pairing: once, at cold start, and never at a foreground.
      const resumed =
        coldStart && stream !== undefined && resumesAtColdStart({ ...facts, unpaired, now });
      if (resumed && stream !== undefined) pair(stream, 'resume');
      const target = reopenTarget({ ...facts, now, resumed });
      if (orphanedSession({ ...facts, now })) unpair('orphan');
      expireOnTheWay(modeStore, current.saved, target, now, logger);
      if (!(target.go === 'stream' && isStreamSubRoute(navigation.current())))
        navigation.go(target.go);
    },
    [modeStore, clock, engine, navigation, logger, unpair, pair],
  );
}

/** Read the target first: expiring removes the code the notice names (R23: never the mode the operator is sent to). */
function expireOnTheWay(
  modeStore: ModeStore,
  saved: SavedState,
  target: ReopenTarget,
  now: Date,
  logger: Logger,
): void {
  const notice = target.go === 'home' ? (target.notice ?? null) : null;
  const expired = expiredModes(saved, now).filter((mode) => mode !== target.go);
  void modeStore
    .expire(expired, notice)
    .catch(() => logger.warn('store.write-refused', { action: 'expire' }));
}
```

- cold start, Idle engine, a saved unexpired code, active `stream`: one `pair` with claim `resume` is sent, and the route is `stream`;
- then `hear({ word: 'replaced' })`: the route is `home` (through `useEngineFollow`) and the code is forgotten; no second `pair` is ever sent (`engine.intents` holds exactly one `pair`);
- a foreground with the engine Idle and the code saved sends no `pair` (the permission-dialog case), and goes Home;
- cold start with the code `tapToPair`, or another mode active, or an expired code, or `unpaired` naming it: no `pair`, Home;
- cold start with the engine already paired (a JS reload while native lived): no `pair`, `stream`.

## Batch C4c — the JS bridge, the routed record and the contract kit

The suite is `pnpm check`, the core suite (Task 27 touches the host), and the bridge project (`CAPTURE_BRIDGE=1 pnpm vitest run --project bridge`), which needs JDK 17 and the host built in C4a.

### Task 25: The JS snapshot wire and the intent wire

Carries 2–6 and CD5, rewritten for the paired snapshot: Task 12's vector file pins both directions, and this task is its JS reader. The old arm wire (old Task 14) goes: the pair intent already is the wire Task 11 maps, so the intent wire is a checked copy, and the P3 language rides in it (Task 23 put it in the intent). Pure functions in the engine module, with no React Native, so they run in the `domain` vitest project.

**Files:**

- Create: `modules/capture-engine/src/snapshotWire.ts`, `modules/capture-engine/src/snapshotWire.test.ts`
- Create: `modules/capture-engine/src/intentWire.ts`, `modules/capture-engine/src/intentWire.test.ts`
- Create: `modules/capture-engine/src/wire/vectorWire.ts` (a case of Task 12's file, merged onto its bases: shared with Task 26's tests), `modules/capture-engine/src/testing/pairIntent.ts` (the made-up `PAIR` intent, shared with Tasks 26 and 27)

Do not touch: `CaptureEnginePort.ts` (Task 23 set its types), the vector file (Task 12 owns it; a mismatch is fixed on both sides, in Task 12's file, with both suites run).

**Interfaces:**

- Consumes `EngineSnapshot`, `EngineIntent`, `PairIntent`, `SessionState`, the `Pairing.ts` types, and `modules/capture-engine/src/wire/snapshot-vectors.json`.
- Produces:

  - `WIRE_VOCABULARY`, one `ReadonlySet` per vocabulary key;
  - `intentWire(intent: EngineIntent): Record<string, unknown>`.

`modules/capture-engine/src/wire/vectorWire.ts`:

```ts
import vectors from './snapshot-vectors.json';

const over = (base: object, patch: object | null | undefined): object | null =>
  patch === null || patch === undefined ? null : { ...base, ...patch };

/** A case's wire as native sends it: its overrides on the shared bases (Task 12's `about`). Throws on an unknown name. */
export function vectorWire(
  name: string,
): Record<string, unknown> & { reportedAtMs: number; pairing: object | null } {
  const found = vectors.cases.find((c) => c.name === name);
  if (found === undefined) throw new Error(`no vector case ${name}`);
  return {
    ...found.wire,
    telemetry: { ...vectors.telemetryBase, ...found.wire.telemetry },
    pairing: over(vectors.pairingBase, found.wire.pairing),
    broadcast: over(vectors.broadcastBase, found.wire.broadcast),
  };
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement** `snapshotWire.ts`:

```ts
import type {
  BroadcastInfo,
  Cause,
  LastEnd,
  NotReady,
  PairingInfo,
  Readiness,
  Refusal,
  Transport,
  Unpaired,
  UnpairReason,
} from '@/domain/session/Pairing';
import type { SessionState } from '@/domain/session/SessionState';
import type { CameraState, EngineSnapshot, Telemetry } from './CaptureEnginePort';

/** Every wire word native writes (Task 12's vocabulary block), checked against the shared file. */
export const WIRE_VOCABULARY = {
  state: new Set([
    'idle',
    'pairing',
    'paired',
    'arming',
    'armed',
    'connecting',
    'publishing',
    'degraded',
    'reconnecting',
    'ended',
  ]),
  transport: new Set(['srt', 'rtmps']),
  reconnectCause: new Set(['uplink-lost', 'video-stalled', 'not-delivered']),
  degradeReason: new Set([
    'not-delivered',
    'camera-taken',
    'mic-silenced',
    'poor-uplink',
    'fell-back-to-rtmps',
  ]),
  endReason: new Set(['operator-stopped', 'fatal-error']),
  cause: new Set(['organiser', 'automatic', 'operator', 'rejoin']),
  notReady: new Set(['camera', 'sound', 'network', 'held']),
  refusal: new Set(['no_destination', 'no_credit', 'not_entitled', 'unknown', 'start-failed']),
  lastEnd: new Set([
    'stopped-by-organiser',
    'stopped-automatically',
    'no-signal',
    'destination-refused',
    'max-duration',
    'phone-lost',
    'ended-by-seazn',
    'hold-window-expired',
    'stopped',
  ]),
  unpairReason: new Set(['code-ended', 'replaced', 'taken', 'permissions']),
  delivery: new Set(['ok', 'stalled', 'unknown']),
  shed: new Set(['overlay-preview', 'preview-framerate', 'encode']),
  heartbeatResult: new Set(['ok', 'failed', 'session-over']),
  connectFailure: new Set(['unresolved', 'refused', 'timeout', 'other']),
  camera: new Set(['own', 'taken', 'reopening', 'resuming', 'switching']),
  thermal: new Set(['none', 'light', 'moderate', 'severe', 'critical', 'emergency', 'shutdown']),
} as const;

type Vocabulary = keyof typeof WIRE_VOCABULARY;
type Wire = Record<string, unknown>;

/** Holds the last pairing and broadcast, by their JSON, so selectors over them stay referentially stable. */
export type WireCache = {
  pairing: { json: string; value: PairingInfo | null } | null;
  broadcast: { json: string; value: BroadcastInfo | null } | null;
};

export const createWireCache = (): WireCache => ({ pairing: null, broadcast: null });

const isObject = (value: unknown): value is Wire =>
  typeof value === 'object' && value !== null && !Array.isArray(value);
const isText = (value: unknown): value is string => typeof value === 'string';
const isNumber = (value: unknown): value is number =>
  typeof value === 'number' && Number.isFinite(value);
const isFlag = (value: unknown): value is boolean => typeof value === 'boolean';
/** A word from `key`'s set, or undefined: undefined is malformed, never a guess. */
function word<T extends string>(key: Vocabulary, value: unknown): T | undefined {
  return isText(value) && WIRE_VOCABULARY[key].has(value as never) ? (value as T) : undefined;
}
/** A word or null; undefined is malformed. */
function wordOrNull<T extends string>(key: Vocabulary, value: unknown): T | null | undefined {
  return value === null ? null : word<T>(key, value);
}

/**
 * Native's `onSnapshot` body → `EngineSnapshot`. A projection, no state
 * machine (AGENTS §2). Null for anything malformed: the bridge keeps the last
 * good snapshot and records the miss, never invents a state.
 */
export function toEngineSnapshot(
  wire: unknown,
  cache: WireCache = createWireCache(),
): EngineSnapshot | null {
  if (!isObject(wire) || !isObject(wire.telemetry) || !isNumber(wire.reportedAtMs)) return null;
  const state = toState(wire.state);
  const ready = toReady(wire.ready);
  const camera = wordOrNull<CameraState>('camera', wire.camera);
  const refusal = wordOrNull<Refusal>('refusal', wire.refusal);
  const lastEnd = wordOrNull<LastEnd>('lastEnd', wire.lastEnd);
  const unpaired = toUnpaired(wire.unpaired);
  const pairing = cached(cache, 'pairing', wire.pairing, toPairing);
  const broadcast = cached(cache, 'broadcast', wire.broadcast, toBroadcast);
  if (state === null || ready === null || camera === undefined || refusal === undefined)
    return null;
  if (
    lastEnd === undefined ||
    unpaired === undefined ||
    pairing === undefined ||
    broadcast === undefined
  )
    return null;
  if (!isFlag(wire.codeEndedPending)) return null;
  return {
    state,
    telemetry: wire.telemetry as Telemetry,
    pairing,
    broadcast,
    ready,
    refusal,
    lastEnd,
    unpaired,
    codeEndedPending: wire.codeEndedPending,
    camera,
    reportedAtMs: wire.reportedAtMs,
    survivesBackground: wire.survivesBackground === true,
  };
}

function toState(value: unknown): SessionState | null {
  if (!isObject(value)) return null;
  const kind = word<SessionState['kind']>('state', value.kind);
  switch (kind) {
    case 'idle':
    case 'pairing':
    case 'paired':
      return { kind };
    case 'arming':
      return arming(value);
    case 'armed':
      return armed(value);
    case 'ended':
      return ended(value);
    case undefined:
      return null;
    default:
      return onAir(kind, value);
  }
}

function arming(value: Wire): SessionState | null {
  const cause = word<Cause>('cause', value.cause);
  return cause !== undefined && isFlag(value.retrying)
    ? { kind: 'arming', cause, retrying: value.retrying }
    : null;
}

function armed(value: Wire): SessionState | null {
  const cause = word<Cause>('cause', value.cause);
  const notReady = wordOrNull<NotReady>('notReady', value.notReady);
  return cause !== undefined && notReady !== undefined ? { kind: 'armed', cause, notReady } : null;
}

function ended(value: Wire): SessionState | null {
  const reason = word<'operator-stopped' | 'fatal-error'>('endReason', value.reason);
  const durationMs =
    value.durationMs === null ? null : isNumber(value.durationMs) ? value.durationMs : undefined;
  return reason !== undefined && durationMs !== undefined
    ? { kind: 'ended', reason, durationMs }
    : null;
}

/** connecting, publishing, degraded and reconnecting: plan A's shapes, unchanged. */
function onAir(
  kind: 'connecting' | 'publishing' | 'degraded' | 'reconnecting',
  value: Wire,
): SessionState | null {
  const transport = word<Transport>('transport', value.transport);
  const since = value.sinceEpochMs;
  if (kind === 'connecting') return transport === undefined ? null : { kind, transport };
  if (kind === 'reconnecting') return reconnecting(value);
  if (transport === undefined || !isNumber(since)) return null;
  if (kind === 'publishing') return { kind, transport, sinceEpochMs: since };
  const reason = word<Extract<SessionState, { kind: 'degraded' }>['reason']>(
    'degradeReason',
    value.reason,
  );
  return reason === undefined ? null : { kind, transport, reason, sinceEpochMs: since };
}

function reconnecting(value: Wire): SessionState | null {
  const cause = word<Extract<SessionState, { kind: 'reconnecting' }>['cause']>(
    'reconnectCause',
    value.cause,
  );
  const { holdRemainingSeconds: left, holdWindowSeconds: window, sinceEpochMs: since } = value;
  if (cause === undefined || !isNumber(left) || !isNumber(window) || !isNumber(since)) return null;
  return {
    kind: 'reconnecting',
    cause,
    holdRemainingSeconds: left,
    holdWindowSeconds: window,
    sinceEpochMs: since,
  };
}

function toReady(value: unknown): Readiness | null {
  if (!isObject(value)) return null;
  const { camera, sound, network, held } = value;
  return isFlag(camera) && isFlag(sound) && isFlag(network) && isFlag(held)
    ? { camera, sound, network, held }
    : null;
}

function toUnpaired(value: unknown): Unpaired | null | undefined {
  if (value === null) return null;
  if (!isObject(value)) return undefined;
  const reason = word<UnpairReason>('unpairReason', value.reason);
  const { code, slot, tokenTag } = value;
  if (reason === undefined || !isText(code) || !isNumber(slot) || !isText(tokenTag))
    return undefined;
  return { reason, code, slot, tokenTag };
}

/** Epoch seconds across the bridge (amendment, The engine port), a Date here. */
function toPairing(value: Wire): PairingInfo | undefined {
  const { code, slot, tokenTag, automatic, label, venueTimezone, scheduledStart, autoAllowed } =
    value;
  const { destinationName, overlayUrl, pollSeconds } = value;
  if (!isText(code) || !isNumber(slot) || !isText(tokenTag) || !isFlag(automatic)) return undefined;
  if (!isText(label) || !isText(venueTimezone) || !isFlag(autoAllowed) || !isNumber(pollSeconds))
    return undefined;
  if (scheduledStart !== null && !isNumber(scheduledStart)) return undefined;
  if (
    (destinationName !== null && !isText(destinationName)) ||
    (overlayUrl !== null && !isText(overlayUrl))
  )
    return undefined;
  const start = scheduledStart === null ? null : new Date(scheduledStart * 1000);
  return {
    code,
    slot,
    tokenTag,
    automatic,
    label,
    venueTimezone,
    scheduledStart: start,
    autoAllowed,
    destinationName,
    overlayUrl,
    pollSeconds,
  };
}

function toBroadcast(value: Wire): BroadcastInfo | undefined {
  const {
    sid,
    playbackUrl,
    overlayUrl,
    label,
    holdWindowSeconds: hold,
    maxDurationMinutes,
    srtOffered,
  } = value;
  const cause = word<Cause>('cause', value.cause);
  const scoreUpdates =
    value.scoreUpdates === 'realtime' || value.scoreUpdates === 'polled'
      ? value.scoreUpdates
      : undefined;
  if (!isText(sid) || cause === undefined || !isText(playbackUrl) || !isText(label))
    return undefined;
  if (
    (overlayUrl !== null && !isText(overlayUrl)) ||
    !isObject(hold) ||
    !isNumber(maxDurationMinutes)
  )
    return undefined;
  if (scoreUpdates === undefined || !isFlag(srtOffered)) return undefined;
  const holdWindowSeconds: Partial<Record<Transport, number>> = {};
  for (const transport of ['srt', 'rtmps'] as const) {
    const seconds = hold[transport];
    if (seconds === undefined) continue;
    if (!isNumber(seconds)) return undefined;
    holdWindowSeconds[transport] = seconds;
  }
  return {
    sid,
    cause,
    playbackUrl,
    overlayUrl,
    label,
    holdWindowSeconds,
    maxDurationMinutes,
    scoreUpdates,
    srtOffered,
  };
}

/** Null stays null; an object is read once per distinct JSON; anything else is malformed (undefined). */
function cached<K extends 'pairing' | 'broadcast'>(
  cache: WireCache,
  key: K,
  value: unknown,
  read: (wire: Wire) => NonNullable<WireCache[K]>['value'] | undefined,
): NonNullable<WireCache[K]>['value'] | undefined {
  if (value === null) return null;
  if (!isObject(value)) return undefined;
  const json = JSON.stringify(value);
  const held = cache[key];
  if (held !== null && held.json === json) return held.value;
  const parsed = read(value);
  if (parsed !== undefined) cache[key] = { json, value: parsed } as WireCache[K];
  return parsed;
}
```

`toPairing` and `toBroadcast` are long field lists, not logic; keep each to its checks, one line a group, and let Prettier wrap them. Telemetry is passed through as native wrote it: the vector test pins every field, and the one rename the spec wanted (`reasons.first()` into `reason`) is native's.

```ts
import type { EngineIntent } from './CaptureEnginePort';

/**
 * An intent as the bridge hands it to native (Task 11's `PairMapping` and
 * `IntentMapping`). Each kind's fields are copied by name, so nothing a caller
 * spread into an intent reaches native, and the pair's token travels only in
 * the field native protects on arrival (Task 20).
 */
export function intentWire(intent: EngineIntent): Record<string, unknown> {
  switch (intent.kind) {
    case 'pair': {
      const {
        code,
        slot,
        token,
        codeUrl,
        heartbeatUrl,
        startUrl,
        language,
        automatic,
        claim,
        environment,
      } = intent;
      return {
        kind: 'pair',
        code,
        slot,
        token,
        codeUrl,
        heartbeatUrl,
        startUrl,
        language,
        automatic,
        claim,
        environment,
      };
    }
    case 'setAutomatic':
      return { kind: 'setAutomatic', on: intent.on };
    case 'setLanguage':
      return { kind: 'setLanguage', language: intent.language };
    default:
      return { kind: intent.kind };
  }
}
```

```ts
// nativeModule.ts
export type Subscription = { remove(): void };
export type CaptureEngineNative = {
  send(intent: Record<string, unknown>): void;
  log(level: string, kind: string, fields: Record<string, unknown>): void;
  current(): unknown;
  tail(): readonly string[];
  addListener(event: 'onSnapshot', listener: (body: unknown) => void): Subscription;
  addListener(event: 'onRecord', listener: (body: { line: string }) => void): Subscription;
  addListener(event: 'onAck', listener: (body: { seq: number }) => void): Subscription;
};
/** `requireOptionalNativeModule('CaptureEngine')`: null on iOS in S1 and in tests (CD23). */

// nativeCaptureEngine.ts
export type ForwardedEntry = {
  readonly level: string;
  readonly event: string;
  readonly fields: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>;
};
export type NativeCaptureEngine = CaptureEnginePort & {
  forward(entry: ForwardedEntry): void;
  /**
   * CD8: resolves once native has acked the last intent sent, so every snapshot that intent
   * caused has arrived. Resolves at once when nothing is outstanding. Test and probe use only;
   * the product never waits on native (AGENTS §2).
   */
  settled(): Promise<void>;
  /** Numbers and sends a non-intent op that native acks (Task 27's host `script` and `readiness`). */
  sendNumbered(op: (seq: number) => void): Promise<void>;
  dispose(): void;
};
export function createNativeCaptureEngine(
  native: CaptureEngineNative,
  deps: { onRecordLine: (line: string) => void },
): NativeCaptureEngine;

// absentCaptureEngine.ts

// sessionRecord.ts
export type RingRecord = SessionRecord & { appendLine(line: string): void };
export function createRoutedRecord(
  ring: RingRecord,
  route: { active(): boolean; forward(entry: LogEntry): void },
): SessionRecord;
/** M16: JS lines go to native's record only while native holds a pairing. Pure, so it is tested. */
export function recordGoesNative(nativeWired: boolean, kind: SessionState['kind']): boolean;
```

- [ ] **Step 1: The module double.** `modules/capture-engine/src/testing/FakeNativeModule.ts`:

```ts
import type { CaptureEngineNative, Subscription } from '../nativeModule';

type Events = { onSnapshot: unknown; onRecord: { line: string }; onAck: { seq: number } };
type Listener = (body: never) => void;

/** A hand-written `CaptureEngineNative`: settable `current` and `tail`, recorded calls, and `emit`. */
export class FakeNativeModule implements CaptureEngineNative {
  readonly sent: Record<string, unknown>[] = [];
  readonly logged: [string, string, Record<string, unknown>][] = [];
  private readonly listeners = new Map<keyof Events, Set<Listener>>();
  /** Runs inside `tail()`, before it returns: D3's race, made deterministic. */
  duringTail: (() => void) | null = null;

  constructor(private readonly state: { current?: unknown; tail?: readonly string[] } = {}) {}

  send(intent: Record<string, unknown>): void {
    this.sent.push(intent);
  }
  log(level: string, kind: string, fields: Record<string, unknown>): void {
    this.logged.push([level, kind, fields]);
  }
  current(): unknown {
    return this.state.current ?? null;
  }
  tail(): readonly string[] {
    this.duringTail?.();
    return this.state.tail ?? [];
  }
  addListener<E extends keyof Events>(event: E, listener: (body: Events[E]) => void): Subscription {
    const set = this.listeners.get(event) ?? new Set<Listener>();
    set.add(listener as Listener);
    this.listeners.set(event, set);
    return { remove: () => set.delete(listener as Listener) };
  }
  emit<E extends keyof Events>(event: E, body: Events[E]): void {
    for (const listener of this.listeners.get(event) ?? [])
      (listener as (body: Events[E]) => void)(body);
  }
  listenerCount(): number {
    return [...this.listeners.values()].reduce((sum, set) => sum + set.size, 0);
  }
}
```

It sits in `src/testing/` so the host adapter (Task 27) and the tests share it; nothing in production imports it, which `grep -rn "testing/FakeNativeModule" src app modules --include=*.ts | grep -v test` checks (empty).

`nativeCaptureEngine.ts`:

```ts
import type { CaptureEnginePort, EngineSnapshot } from './CaptureEnginePort';
import { intentWire } from './intentWire';
import type { CaptureEngineNative, Subscription } from './nativeModule';
import { UNREPORTED } from './unreported';
import { createWireCache, toEngineSnapshot } from './snapshotWire';

export function createNativeCaptureEngine(
  native: CaptureEngineNative,
  deps: { onRecordLine: (line: string) => void },
): NativeCaptureEngine {
  const cache = createWireCache();
  const listeners = new Set<() => void>();
  let snapshot: EngineSnapshot = toEngineSnapshot(native.current(), cache) ?? UNREPORTED;
  const acks = createAcks();
  const subscriptions = listen(native, {
    snapshot: (body) => {
      const next = toEngineSnapshot(body, cache);
      if (next === null) return;
      snapshot = next;
      for (const listener of listeners) listener();
    },
    ack: acks.acked,
  });
  subscriptions.push(seedRecord(native, deps.onRecordLine));
  return {
    send: (intent) => acks.next((seq) => native.send({ ...intentWire(intent), seq })),
    sendNumbered: (op) => {
      acks.next(op);
      return acks.settled();
    },
    subscribe: (onChange) => {
      listeners.add(onChange);
      return () => listeners.delete(onChange);
    },
    getSnapshot: () => snapshot,
    forward: (entry) => native.log(entry.level, entry.event, { ...entry.fields }),
    settled: acks.settled,
    dispose: () => {
      for (const subscription of subscriptions) subscription.remove();
      acks.release();
    },
  };
}

/**
 * D3: listen first, buffer what arrives, read the tail, then hand on the tail
 * and every buffered line the tail does not already end with. A line written
 * while the tail was read is in one or the other, never both, never neither.
 */
function seedRecord(native: CaptureEngineNative, onLine: (line: string) => void): Subscription {
  let buffer: string[] | null = [];
  const subscription = native.addListener('onRecord', ({ line }) => {
    if (buffer === null) onLine(line);
    else buffer.push(line);
  });
  const tail = native.tail();
  const early = buffer;
  buffer = null;
  tail.forEach(onLine);
  for (const line of early) if (!tail.includes(line)) onLine(line);
  return subscription;
}

function listen(
  native: CaptureEngineNative,
  on: { snapshot: (body: unknown) => void; ack: (seq: number) => void },
): Subscription[] {
  return [
    native.addListener('onSnapshot', on.snapshot),
    native.addListener('onAck', ({ seq }) => on.ack(seq)),
  ];
}

/** CD8's sequence numbers: the last sent, the highest acked, and the waiters on it. */
function createAcks() {
  let sent = 0;
  let acked = 0;
  let waiters: { target: number; resolve: () => void }[] = [];
  const wake = () => {
    const due = waiters.filter((waiter) => waiter.target <= acked);
    waiters = waiters.filter((waiter) => waiter.target > acked);
    for (const waiter of due) waiter.resolve();
  };
  return {
    next: (send: (seq: number) => void) => {
      sent += 1;
      send(sent);
    },
    acked: (seq: number) => {
      acked = Math.max(acked, seq);
      wake();
    },
    settled: () =>
      sent <= acked
        ? Promise.resolve()
        : new Promise<void>((resolve) => waiters.push({ target: sent, resolve })),
    release: () => {
      acked = sent;
      wake();
    },
  };
}
```

`includes` compares by the line's text, which is what D3 asked for: native's lines carry their own `at`, so two distinct lines are never equal. `UNREPORTED` moves to `modules/capture-engine/src/unreported.ts`: the idle snapshot, every field at rest (`pairing`, `broadcast`, `refusal`, `lastEnd`, `unpaired` null, `codeEndedPending` false, `ready` all false, `camera` null, `reportedAtMs: 0`, `survivesBackground: false`) and `IDLE_TELEMETRY`, which moves from `FakeCaptureEngine.ts` into `unreported.ts` and is imported back into the fake, so production code never imports the fake.

`absentCaptureEngine.ts`:

```ts
import { tokenTag } from '@/domain/credentials/tokenTag';
import type { PairingInfo } from '@/domain/session/Pairing';
import type { CaptureEnginePort, EngineSnapshot, PairIntent } from './CaptureEnginePort';
import { UNREPORTED } from './unreported';

/** What an absent engine names a code by: the intent's name, and nothing the claim would have told it. */
const namedBy = (intent: PairIntent): PairingInfo => ({
  code: intent.code,
  slot: intent.slot,
  tokenTag: tokenTag(intent.token),
  automatic: intent.automatic,
  label: '',
  venueTimezone: '',
  scheduledStart: null,
  autoAllowed: false,
  destinationName: null,
  overlayUrl: null,
  pollSeconds: 60,
});

/**
 * CD23: the port with no native module behind it. Three snapshots and no
 * timers: idle, ended fatal-error naming the code a `pair` sent, idle again
 * after `reset`. Every other intent is ignored, as native ignores one that
 * does not fit (AGENTS §2).
 */
export function createAbsentCaptureEngine(now: () => number): CaptureEnginePort {
  const listeners = new Set<() => void>();
  let snapshot: EngineSnapshot = { ...UNREPORTED, reportedAtMs: now() };
  const show = (next: Partial<EngineSnapshot>) => {
    snapshot = { ...snapshot, ...next, reportedAtMs: now() };
    for (const listener of listeners) listener();
  };
  return {
    send: (intent) => {
      const kind = snapshot.state.kind;
      if (intent.kind === 'pair' && kind === 'idle') {
        show({
          state: { kind: 'ended', reason: 'fatal-error', durationMs: null },
          pairing: namedBy(intent),
        });
      }
      if (intent.kind === 'reset' && kind === 'ended')
        show({ state: { kind: 'idle' }, pairing: null });
    },
    subscribe: (onChange) => {
      listeners.add(onChange);
      return () => listeners.delete(onChange);
    },
    getSnapshot: () => snapshot,
  };
}
```

`sessionRecord.ts`: `createRingRecord` gains `appendLine(line)`, which pushes a pre-formatted line under the same capacity rule; `createRoutedRecord` appends to the ring when `route.active()` is false and forwards otherwise, and delegates `lines` and `subscribe` to the ring (native's lines arrive through `appendLine`, so the ring is still the one view); and:

Task 23 wrote the kit as data and ran it on the fake; this task runs it through the real JS bridge (Task 26) over the real Kotlin core (Task 21's JVM host), server words included, and adds the two ordering scenarios plan A's final review asked for. Pre-flight **P8** and **D4** are folded: the workflow has plain triggers, `concurrency` and `permissions: contents: read`, as `kotlin-core.yml` does.

**Files:**

- Modify: `modules/capture-engine/src/contract/engineScenarios.ts` (`ScenarioKit.sendTogether`; carries 27 and 28)
- Modify: `test/engineContract.ts` (`sendTogether` in the wrapper's kit)
- Modify (Kotlin, the host only): `modules/capture-engine/android/core/host/src/main/kotlin/com/seazn/capture/engine/host/Host.kt`, `ScriptedServer.kt`, `ScriptedPlatform.kt`, `ExecutorScheduler.kt`, and `host/src/test/.../ProtocolTest.kt` (`script` and `readiness` take an optional `seq`, acked once the host is quiet; `readiness` gains `network`; `WAITING.pollSeconds` 5)
- Create: `test/hostEngine.ts` (spawns the host; an `EngineUnderTest` over `createNativeCaptureEngine`)
- Create: `test/serverScript.ts` (`ServerSays` → the host's `script` line)
- Create: `modules/capture-engine/src/NativeCaptureEngine.bridge.test.ts`
- Modify: `vitest.config.mts` (a `bridge` project behind `CAPTURE_BRIDGE=1`; `**/*.bridge.test.ts` excluded from `domain`)
- Create: `.github/workflows/bridge-contract.yml`. `kotlin-core.yml` is untouched: its header and spec §6 say JDK 17 and Gradle and nothing else (I11)

Do not touch: the core's `src/main` (native is the authority, AGENTS §2: a disagreement is fixed in the JS bridge, the mapping, the fake or the host's script, never in the core to suit a test).

**Interfaces:**

- Consumes `ENGINE_SCENARIOS`, `ScenarioKit`, `ServerSays`, `EngineUnderTest`, `describeEngineContract`, `createNativeCaptureEngine`, `NativeCaptureEngine.sendNumbered`, `FakeNativeModule`'s shape, Task 21's host protocol.
- Produces `ScenarioKit.sendTogether(intents)`, `EngineUnderTest.settle?`, `startHostEngine(): Promise<EngineUnderTest>`, `scriptFor(says): { path; status; body }`, and the host ops `{"op":"script","seq":n,…}` and `{"op":"readiness","seq":n,"camera"?,"audioPeak"?,"pose"?,"network"?}`.

**How the kit's three verbs reach the host.**

| Kit verb         | Host line                                              | Acked when                                                                      |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `send(intent)`   | `{"op":"send","seq":n,"intent":…}`                     | after the intent's own tasks (Task 21, CD8)                                     |
| `say(words)`     | `{"op":"script","seq":n,"path":…,"status":…,"body":…}` | after the next request on that path has been answered **and** the host is quiet |
| `ready(partial)` | `{"op":"readiness","seq":n,…}`                         | once the host is quiet                                                          |

"Quiet" is: no scripted HTTP request in flight, and no task due now on the core's scheduler. A Go live is a chain — the beat's answer, the code fetch, Armed, the platform's connect — on two executors, so an ack after the beat answer alone would let the kit read Arming. Quiet waits for the chain, and never for a timer that is not yet due (the next beat, the 500 ms tick), so it cannot wait forever. `say` is bounded by the beat cadence: `WAITING.pollSeconds` is 5, `BeatCadence`'s floor (Task 3), so a say is heard within 5 s.

`ServerSays` → script, per the amendment's _Contract shapes_ and Task 3's `ServerWord` rows:

| `ServerSays`        | path    | status | body                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ------------------- | ------- | ------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `go-live {cause}`   | `beat`  | 200    | `WAITING` with `state: "go-live"`, `sid: "sess_host"`, `startedBy: cause`                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `live`              | `beat`  | 200    | `{state: "live", sid: "sess_host"}`                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `over {lastEnd}`    | `beat`  | 200    | `{state: "over", sid: "sess_host", endReason}`, `endReason` the server word `LastEnd.of` reads back to `lastEnd` (`stopped-by-organiser` → `stopped`, and so on; `hold-window-expired` and `stopped` have no server word and are refused by `scriptFor`) |
| `refused {refusal}` | `start` | 402    | `{code: refusal, message: "scripted"}`; heard at the next operator start, not at once                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `replaced`          | `beat`  | 200    | `{state: "replaced"}`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `taken`             | `beat`  | 200    | `{state: "taken"}`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `code-ended`        | `beat`  | 401    | `{code: "code_ended", message: "scripted"}`                                                                                                                                                                                                              |

`refused` on the host is acked when the start is answered, so a kit scenario says it, then sends `start`, then reads. No scenario in `ENGINE_SCENARIOS` uses it today; the row exists so the one that does cannot misread the fake's at-once refusal as native's.

`hostWithEvents()` builds a `Host` over a real `ExecutorScheduler` with `write` collecting events as `"ack:n"` for acks and the snapshot body's state kind for snapshots; `awaitEvent(name, timeoutMs = 3_000)` polls every 20 ms and fails with the events seen. Then:

- `ExecutorScheduler` gains `fun dueNow(): Int`: the executor queue's tasks whose delay is ≤ 0, plus 1 while a task runs (a counter around each task's body).
- `ScriptedServer` gains `@Volatile var inFlight: Int`, raised in `answer` before it answers and lowered by the platform once the answer is handed to the core, and `fun onAnswered(path: String, then: () -> Unit)`, a one-shot run after that path's next answer is handed over. `WAITING`'s `pollSeconds` becomes 5.
- `ScriptedServer.path` reads any `https://stg.seazn.club/api/capture/codes/<code>` URL with a query as `code` (Task 21 matched only `host-code`), and the code answer's `code` field is the `<code>` the URL names, so the kit's `kit-a` and `kit-b` fetch their own session shape. A `ScriptedServerTest` case pins both: `kit-a?slot=1&phone=p` answers 200 with `code` `kit-a`.
- `Host` gains `private fun whenQuiet(seq: Int)`, which polls every 20 ms on its own single-thread executor until `server.inFlight == 0 && scheduler.dueNow() == 0`, then posts `platform.acked(seq)` on the core's scheduler at delay 0 (so it is written after anything already posted). `handle` reads `seq` on `script` and `readiness`: `script` with a `seq` calls `server.script(...)` then `server.onAnswered(path) { whenQuiet(seq) }`; `readiness` with a `seq` calls `core.readiness(...)` (and `core.network(...)` when `network` is present), then `whenQuiet(seq)`.
- `pose` reads `"left"`, `"right"`, `"not-held"` and `"no-sensor"` as Task 21 has it; `camera` false reports no frames; `audioPeak` 0 is below the floor.
